en.header: India's TCS, Transamerica end $2 bln contract due to macro environment
en.content: BENGALURU, June 16 (Reuters) - Indian information technology (IT) company Tata Consultancy Services (TCS.NS) said on Friday it has mutually agreed with insurance provider Transamerica to end a $2 billion contract, citing reasons including a challenging macro environment.The 10-year contract, signed in early 2018, involved TCS working with U.S.-based Transameria to enable the digitization of more than 10 million policies into a single integrated platform.Administration of those policies, including life insurance and retirement and investment solutions, will be moved to a new servicing model, which will take about 30 months, TCS said."It's more of a sentimental negative rather than a big impact on the financials of TCS," said Siddhartha Khemka, head of retail research at Motilal Oswal Financial Services.Indian IT companies, which draw a bulk of their revenue from the United States and Europe, have flagged a slowdown in the telecom and communication segment as clients contemplate spending cuts and project rampdowns to save cash."We don't see a big impact because of this. But yes, it's a sign that the demand environment is not very good" Khemka said.TCS stock is currently trading 1.3% lower at 3,175 rupees.Reporting by Navamya Ganesh Acharya in Bengaluru; Editing by Rashmi Aich and Sonia CheemaOur Standards: The Thomson Reuters Trust Principles.
en.summary: Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) has agreed with Transamerica to end a $2bn contract signed in 2018, citing challenges in the macro environment. The Indian IT firm said it will move more than 10 million policies, including life insurance, investment and retirement solutions to a new servicing model over 30 months.

record.header: Analysis: Thai stocks flounder in absence of China spark
record.content: SINGAPORE, June 16 (Reuters) - Thailand's stock market has become the symbol of investor disenchantment with China's economic reopening, going from market darling in January to Asia's second-worst performing market by June, with little sign of a turnaround.Not only has the promised export boom and tourism boost from China's return after 3 years of pandemic lockdowns failed to materialise, a political logjam at home has become another drag on the SET index (.SETI).After a jump in early January, the market is now down more than 6% for the year, second in losses only to Malaysia."I'm surprised that we're struggling," said Jeep Chatikavanij, portfolio manager at Bangkok-based Ton Poh Fund."At the beginning of the year, I thought we were going to have wind in our sails. Our view was that the dollar has peaked, the Fed is done raising, and tourism is going to boost the economy.""Although a lot of that has happened, particularly on the tourism front, we haven't seen the trickle down effect that we anticipated," Jeep said.The biggest setback has been the rocky and uneven Chinese recovery. China is the largest consumer of Thailand's exports, particularly agricultural products. Those grew just 3.9% in the January-April period, as the pandemic-driven demand for electronics that spurred double-digit growth during the previous two years faded.Thailand recorded a current account deficit of $0.5 billion in April, reversing a $4.8 billion surplus in the previous month, as exports contracted 4.9% year-on-year."We think China's weaker reopening momentum has had significant impact on the performance of Thai assets this year," said Pruksa Iamthongthong, senior investment director of Asian equities at abrdn, who is underweight on Thailand in the firm's flagship regional fund."Domestically, concerns have been around the impact of China's stalling recovery on the Thai economy. This has been reflected in the latest trade and export data."Foreign investment out of the $550 billion Thai stock market stood at $995 million in May, marking the fourth straight month of outflows, the longest such streak in two years, data from Refinitiv showed.They had rushed in early in 2023, spurred by a wave of optimism following China's exit from its zero-COVID regime. The Thai baht rallied 15% from its October low to a high of 32.565 per dollar in January. It now fetches 34.67 per dollar.The stock market too touched a nine-month peak in January before giving up most of its gains.POLITICAL ANGSTAt home, Thailand's politics have sapped sentiment after a progressive opposition Move Forward party and Pheu Thai parties thumped conservative opponents allied with the military, fuelling hope for an end to nearly nine years of army-backed rule.But a government has yet to be formed, while a prime minister is expected to be selected only in August as frontrunner Pita Limjareonrat faces setbacks and challenges."You need to attach a certain level of political premium to Thai assets until we know which party is going to take over and importantly, who the new prime minister will be," said Johnny Chen, portfolio manager at William Blair's emerging markets debt team."As of now, there's still quite a high degree of uncertainty," said Chen, whose fund had reduced its Thailand exposure prior to the elections as valuations became less attractive.Amidst those hitches, Thailand's tourism industry remains a bright spot.The country received 11.4 million foreign tourist arrivals from January to June 11, and saw spending of 472 billion baht ($13.67 billion), surpassing the 11.15 million arrivals in the whole of 2022.The government expects at least 25 million foreign visitors in 2023. That has also somewhat been reflected in the stock market, with the SET Tourism and Leisure Index less impacted than the broader gauge and slightly up on the year."We do expect Thailand's economic recovery to continue this year as tourism rebounds, and that should support the economy, private consumption, anchor domestic demand and also anchor Thailand's external balances," said William Blair's Chen."In the medium term, we still think there's some potential to re-enter Thai assets."(This story has been refiled to fix a typographical error in paragraph 1)Reporting by Rae Wee in Singapore and Patturaja Murugaboopathy in Bengaluru; additional reporting by Ankur Banerjee in Singapore and Gaurav Dogra in BengaluruEditing by Vidya Ranganathan & Shri NavaratnamOur Standards: The Thomson Reuters Trust Principles.
record.summary: Thailand's stock market has become the second-worst performing market in Asia due to a lack of the anticipated export boom, tourism boost from China's reopening, and a political logjam at home, which has become another drag on the SET index. China is the largest consumer of Thailand's exports, particularly agricultural products, and a weaker reopening momentum in China has had a significant impact on the performance of Thai assets this year.

en.header: UK public's inflation expectations ease in May, Bank of England survey shows
en.content: LONDON, June 16 (Reuters) - The British public's expectations for inflation in the coming 12 months cooled in May, according to a Bank of England survey on Friday that also showed net satisfaction with the central bank hit its lowest level since records began in 1999.The BoE's quarterly inflation attitudes survey showed expectations for inflation in the coming 12 months fell to 3.5% from 3.9% in February.For inflation in five years' time, expectations were steady at 3.0%.The survey was conducted in mid-May, before recent inflation and jobs data sent expectations in financial markets for more BoE interest rate hikes sharply higher - with a big knock-on effect in mortgage costs.The BoE is watching gauges of inflation expectations closely. Recent surveys of the public and businesses suggest inflation expectations have cooled in recent months, but remain above their long-run average.Friday's survey showed the public's net satisfaction with how well the BoE is controlling inflation fell to a new record low of -13%, from -4% previously.Consumer price inflation dropped in April to 8.7% from 10.1% in March, but it was still the joint-highest rate among major advanced economies, alongside Italy.The survey, conducted by polling firm Ipsos, was conducted between May 12 and May 16.Reporting by Andy Bruce; editing by David MillikenOur Standards: The Thomson Reuters Trust Principles.
en.summary: The British public's expectations for inflation in the next 12 months have dropped to 3.5% from 3.9% in February, according to a Bank of England survey. However, satisfaction with the central bank has hit its lowest level since records began in 1999.

record.content: LONDON, June 15 (Reuters) - The smallest proportion of businesses since at least March last year expect to raise prices next month, a survey of businesses showed on Thursday.The Office for National Statistics showed 17.0% of companies that are currently trading expected to raise prices in the coming month, down from 17.7% in the previous month.It was the lowest reading since the ONS first published the data series in March 2022.Reporting by Andy Bruce; editing by David MillikenOur Standards: The Thomson Reuters Trust Principles.

en.header: BoE to quiz non-banks over market risks soon - FPC's Breeden
en.subheader: The Bank of England will launch an exercise very soon to test how non-bank financial institutions' react to market stress, senior BoE regulator Sarah Breeden said on Friday.
en.content: LONDON, June 16 (Reuters) - The Bank of England will launch an exercise very soon to test how non-bank financial institutions' react to market stress, senior BoE regulator Sarah Breeden said on Friday."The Bank is very shortly launching its exploratory exercise to enhance understanding of the risks to and from non-banks, their behaviours, and how these behaviours can amplify shocks," Breeden told a financial services conference in London.Breeden said the BoE would give more details about the exercise next week.Reporting by David Milliken; editing by William JamesOur Standards: The Thomson Reuters Trust Principles.
en.summary: The Bank of England will conduct an exploratory exercise to test non-bank financial institutions' reactions to market stress, according to senior BoE regulator Sarah Breeden. The exercise aims to enhance understanding of the risks to and from non-banks, their behaviours and how these behaviours can amplify shocks.

record.content: LONDON, June 14 (Reuters) - The Bank of England is weighing up whether to raise interest rates for the 13th meeting in a row next week as it continues to grapple with one of the highest inflation rates among the world's big, rich countries.Investors think it is a near-certainty that the BoE will announce a rate increase of at least a quarter-percentage point on June 22, taking Bank Rate to 4.75%, and a roughly 20% chance of a half-point rise to 5%.Following is a summary of recent comments by members of the Monetary Policy Committee.MPC MEMBERS WHO VOTED IN MAY FOR A 25 BASIS-POINT HIKEANDREW BAILEY, GOVERNORJune 13: "We still think the rate of inflation is going to come down, but its taking a lot longer than expected."He said British food price inflation had been slower to drop than global commodity prices, despite past reassurances from the Bank's contacts in the retail industry that prices would fall. "We've been told for some time, you know, they've reached their peak, they're going to come down, the rate of inflation is going to come down. And then the contacts come back and say 'Sorry, we got that one wrong.'"May 23: On interest rates, he said: "I can't tell you whether we're near to the peak, I can't tell you whether we are at the peak. I think we are nearer to the peak than we were."BEN BROADBENT, DEPUTY GOVERNORMay 11: "A lot of ... global prices are declining.""And we expect for that reason predominantly - so independently of the rate of unemployment - (that) that will bring down wage growth."DAVE RAMSDEN, DEPUTY GOVERNORMay 18: "There is more of a concern (among investors) about persistence of inflation (in Britain) and therefore an expectation that our short-term rate - set by us - will be higher. That feeds through into yields"JON CUNLIFFE, DEPUTY GOVERNORHas not commented on monetary policy in recent months.HUW PILL, CHIEF ECONOMISTMay 12: He said there was evidence of a "more favourable pattern in terms of the inflation outlook" but "there may be more work to do.""To the extend that we see elements of greater persistence, there may be scope, at least to continue with the tightening of policy we have at the moment.""If we were to see more evidence that inflation is falling and most inflationary pressures are easing ... then the outlook for interest rates would be different."CATHERINE MANN, EXTERNAL MPC MEMBERJune 12: She said central banks like the BoE could find it hard to communicate the end of their rate-tightening cycle. "Fine-tuning is something that monetary policy is not very good at if the ultimate objective is to focus on inflation.""I called it the policy boogie ... you hike, you cut, you hold and you're just kind of giving signals that are hard to determine and hard for the market to understand why you're doing it.""Inflation expectations, in fact, are on the downswing even as some of these core and services prints have been more robust than we would have hoped for."JONATHAN HASKEL, EXTERNAL MPC MEMBERJune 12: He said the BoE is "closely monitoring" indicators of inflation momentum and persistence, in an article for the Scotsman newspaper. "My own view is that it is important we continue to lean against the risks of inflation momentum, and therefore that further increases in interest rates cannot be ruled out."May 25: "I prefer to lean against the risks of inflation momentum. As difficult as our current circumstances are, embedded inflation would be worse."MPC MEMBERS WHO VOTED IN MAY TO STOP RAISING RATESSWATI DHINGRA, EXTERNAL MPC MEMBERJune 13: "The lags in monetary policy transmission imply that there is little we can do to affect inflation in the immediate future.""There are reasons to suspect that policy transmission will be slower than previous cycles."SILVANA TENREYRO, EXTERNAL MPC MEMBERApril 14: "We need to be patient (to see the effects of past rate increases). We don't want to get burned. We don't want to get an ice-cold shower."Compiled by Suban Abdulla; editing by David MillikenOur Standards: The Thomson Reuters Trust Principles.
record.header: Bank of England policymakers consider 13th successive rate rise
record.summary: The Bank of England is considering raising interest rates for the 13th consecutive meeting next week due to high inflation rates compared to other wealthy countries. Analysts believe that the likelihood of a quarter-point increase is almost certain, with a 20% chance of a half-point rise.

ru.header: Банк Англии в ближайшее время проведет опрос небанковских банков по поводу рыночных рисков - Breeden от FPC
ru.subheader: Банк Англии очень скоро начнет учения, чтобы проверить, как небанковские финансовые учреждения реагируют на рыночный стресс, заявила в пятницу старший регулятор Банка Англии Сара Бриден.
ru.content: LONDON, June 16 (Reuters) - The Bank of England will launch an exercise very soon to test how non-bank financial institutions' react to market stress, senior BoE regulator Sarah Breeden said on Friday."The Bank is very shortly launching its exploratory exercise to enhance understanding of the risks to and from non-banks, their behaviours, and how these behaviours can amplify shocks," Breeden told a financial services conference in London.Breeden said the BoE would give more details about the exercise next week.Reporting by David Milliken; editing by William JamesOur Standards: The Thomson Reuters Trust Principles.
ru.summary: По словам старшего регулятора Банка Англии Сары Бриден, Банк Англии проведет исследовательское мероприятие для проверки реакции небанковских финансовых учреждений на рыночный стресс. Цель этого мероприятия - улучшить понимание рисков, связанных с небанковскими организациями и исходящих от них, их поведения и того, как это поведение может усилить потрясения.

As difficult as our current circumstances are, embedded inflation would be worse."MPC MEMBERS WHO VOTED IN MAY TO STOP RAISING RATESSWATI DHINGRA, EXTERNAL MPC MEMBERJune 13: "The lags in monetary policy transmission imply that there is little we can do to affect inflation in the immediate future.""There are reasons to suspect that policy transmission will be slower than previous cycles."SILVANA TENREYRO, EXTERNAL MPC MEMBERApril 14: "We need to be patient (to see the effects of past rate increases). We don't want to get burned. We don't want to get an ice-cold shower."Compiled by Suban Abdulla; editing by David MillikenOur Standards: The Thomson Reuters Trust Principles.
record.header: Bank of England policymakers consider 13th successive rate rise
record.summary: The Bank of England is considering raising interest rates for the 13th consecutive meeting next week due to high inflation rates compared to other wealthy countries. Analysts believe that the likelihood of a quarter-point increase is almost certain, with a 20% chance of a half-point rise.

en.header: VTB expects profit in 2023 at the level of 400 billion rubles
en.subheader: VTB can earn a profit of about 400 billion rubles this year, and it can also be quite successful in 2024, the head of the bank, Andrei Kostin, said at SPIEF.
en.content: Moscow. On 16 June, INTERFAX.RU - WTB can make profits of about 400 billion roubles this year, and in 2024 it can also be quite successful, declared to PMEF the head of the Bank of Andrei Costin. "This year we are prepared to show profits of about 400 billion. In fact, we believe that next year may also be quite successful according to our projections, but the problems remain," he said. The WTB projected net returns under IFRS in 2023 ranging from 327 billion to 400 billion roubles after a record loss of 613 billion roubles.
en.summary: The head of VTB Andrey Kostin said that the bank can earn about 400 billion rubles of profit this year and predicts a successful 2024. However, problems remain, including after a record loss of 613 billion rubles in 2020.

record.header: Rostelecom will launch a new venture fund of 8 billion rubles
record.subheader: Rostelecom plans to launch a new venture fund with a limit of 8 billion rubles in the near future, First Vice President, financial Director of the company Sergey Anokhin said at SPIEF.
record.content: Moscow. June 15, INTERFAX.RU, Rostelecom, is about to launch a new venture fund with a limit of 8 billion roubles, reported to PMEF by the First Vice-President, the financial director of Sergei Anohin. "The fund's Limite is now set at 8 billion roubles. This is an investment in addition to our existing fund (Commit Capital-IF) and the investment plans for the new digital business," Anohin explained, and he said that the new fund would focus on supporting domestic Internet services, digital platforms, industrial software developers. He added that the fund would focus on those companies that had passed through the industrial centres of competence in the import of software. The Fund will invest in such companies, both on its own and in collaboration with other major players. He also reported that the current Committ Capital venture fund planned to invest some 13 billion roubles in more mature companies that had already "sniffed" their niches in the next three years. The foundation, established in 2015, was transformed last year into a management company format to develop new digital business by Rostelecoma, said CFO to the operator. "Optimized (F.F.F.F.F. ) last year, just in the wake of the emergence of new windows of opportunity, market dynamics, we began to look actively at what other digital areas Rostelecom could offer value to its clients," noted Anohin. Since its inception in 2015, the Fund has invested approximately 2 billion roubles directly into companies and 2 billion roubles directly into the Internet Initiative Development Fund (FRII) in 2020.
record.summary: Rostelecom plans to launch a new venture fund for 8 billion rubles, which will focus on supporting domestic Internet services, digital platforms and industrial software developers. The current venture capital fund "CommIT Capital" plans to invest 13 billion rubles in more mature companies in the next 3 years to develop new digital businesses of Rostelecom.

ru.header: ВТБ ожидает прибыль в 2023 году на уровне 400 млрд рублей
ru.subheader: ВТБ может заработать в этом году прибыль в размере около 400 млрд рублей, в 2024 году также может быть достаточно успешным, заявил на ПМЭФ глава банка Андрей Костин.
ru.content: Москва. 16 июня. INTERFAX.RU - ВТБ может заработать в этом году прибыль в размере около 400 млрд рублей, в 2024 году также может быть достаточно успешным, заявил на ПМЭФ глава банка Андрей Костин."В этом году мы готовы показать прибыль порядка 400 млрд. В общем-то считаем, что следующий год тоже может быть достаточно успешным по нашим прогнозам, но проблемы остаются", - сказал он.ВТБ в 2023 году прогнозировал чистую прибыль по МСФО в диапазоне от 327 млрд до 400 млрд рублей после рекордного убытка в 613 млрд рублей.
ru.summary: Глава ВТБ Андрей Костин заявил, что банк может заработать около 400 млрд рублей прибыли в этом году и прогнозирует успешный 2024 год. Однако остаются проблемы, в том числе после рекордного убытка в 613 млрд рублей в 2020 году.

en.subheader: Sberbank opened ATMs in Crimea, calculations of the S-300 air defense systems worked out repelling attacks in the Moscow region, Turkey canceled the visit of the Swedish Defense Minister.
en.content: On 21 January, INTERFAX.RU, a summary of events that had taken place in the country.- The Russian Ministry of Defence reported that more than 150 soldiers, more than 30 weapons, military and special equipment had been deployed to the Ministry of Defence of the Russian Federation. Russian woman Ekaterina Alexandrov gave way to the representative of Poland, Magda Lynette, in the third round of the tournament.

Россиянка Екатерина Александрова уступила представительнице Польши Магде Линетт в третьем круге турнира.

en.header: Arestovich doubted the guaranteed victory of Ukraine
en.subheader: Ex-adviser to the office of the President Arestovich doubted the guaranteed victory of Ukraine
en.content: A former adviser to the office of the President of Ukraine, Alexei Arrestovich, said that Kiev could lose a special military operation launched by Russia, which he said in an interview to journalist and political scientist Yuri Romanenko, which was published on the YouTube Canal of Arrestovich. He recalled the words of President Andrzej Duda of Poland in Davos that it might soon be decisive for the outcome of the conflict in Ukraine. "We are within a very clear special operation of the Russians for us <...> And the Polish president will say that now the months of decision in Ukraine are unknown, because they understand what is going to happen. "Before we giggle over the bad Russians and rejoice that we're invincible, I remind you, we're invincible until we start racing with each other. When we started racing with each other, we were very defeated, won quickly, and suddenly for ourselves," he continued. "And if everyone thinks that I'm an informal person now, I can say everything I want to say, if everyone thinks we're gonna win a war, it's very different. From the 14th, it's no longer like it's like it's going to be very, very strong," he said, "and if everyone thinks that I'm an unofficial person now, I can say anything I want to say, if everyone thinks we're gonna win a war, it's very different. The material is being supplemented.

record.header: In the Kremlin, there was a rise in the spiral conflict around Ukraine.
record.subheader: President Dmitri Peskov's press secretary assessed the conflict around Ukraine as emerging from the spiral.
record.content: Moscow. On 20 January, INTERFAX.RU, President Dmitry Peskov's press secretary, assessed the conflict around Ukraine as emerging from the spiral. He was asked at the briefing whether it was possible to say that the escalation of the conflict was on the rise. "As we see that it is indeed developing along the upward spiral," he replied. "We see the growing indirect and sometimes direct involvement of the countries of NATO in this conflict. We hear statements that indicate the absolute domination of the political will to continue this engagement. We see a commitment to the dramatic delusion of Ukraine's ability to have some success in the battlefield," he continued. "This is a dramatic delusion of the Western community that will make it regretable again and again," noted Peskov. "We are sure and there can be no doubt about it." In his view, "it does cause the conflict to degenerate and cause additional tension in the rising spiral." In order to reduce escalation, Peskov pointed out, we must listen to Russia. "We need to listen to Russia's concerns, we need to internally "recover the film" to the end, I would say, of the year before last, when Russia offered to discuss its concerns at the negotiating table and when Russia was completely rejected," said Peskov. He pointed out that "of course, we must repent, perhaps in cynicism, in the last eight years when the game of pips took place, there is such a game of pips when both the FRG and France and Ukraine played "in puffs" with the Mina arrangements, but now they're paying for it." The press secretary of the President of the Russian Federation stressed the need to understand all the negative consequences of this game, which they played, "swindling Moscow, deceiving the people of Donbas, and trying to prepare for them a more terrible fate, which Russia prevented and prevented". He also said that supplying Ukraine with heavy tanks would not change anything in terms of the Russian side ' s progress towards achieving its objectives. "The consequences will be a negative sign, definitely. We have repeatedly said that such transfers will not make a fundamental difference. They would add problems to Ukraine and the Ukrainian people, said the representative of the Kremlin. It is not appropriate to exaggerate the importance of such transfers in terms of their ability to change; experts are well aware of all the problems that accompany such transfers; all these tanks need to be maintained and repaired." He stressed that "the problem in Ukraine will add to it, but will not change anything in terms of the Russian side's progress towards achieving its objectives".

ru.header: Арестович усомнился в гарантированной победе Украины
ru.subheader: Экс-советник офиса президента Арестович усомнился в гарантированной победе Украины
ru.content: Бывший советник офиса президента Украины Алексей Арестович заявил, что Киев может проиграть в специальной военной операции, начатой Россией. Об этом он заявил в интервью журналисту и политологу Юрию Романенко, оно опубликовано на YouTube-канале Арестовича.Он вспомнил слова президента Польши Анджея Дуды, сказанные в Давосе, о том, что ближайшее время может быть решающим для исхода конфликта на Украине.«Мы внутри очень четкой спецоперации россиян по нам <...> И польский президент произонсит, что сейчас решающие месяцы по Украине, неизвестно, что будет, потому что они понимают, что затевается. Герасимова поставили <...)», — сказал Арестович.«Прежде, чем хихикать над дурными русскими, и радоваться, что мы непобедимы, напоминаю, мы непобедимы до тех пор, пока мы не начали грызться друг с другом. Когда мы начали грызться друг с другом, мы очень победимые, победимые в кратчайшие сроки, и неожиданно для самих себя», — продолжил он.«И если все думают, что — я сейчас неофициальное лицо уже, могу говорить все, что хочу — если все думают, что мы гарантированно выиграем войну, то очень непохоже. С 14 числа уже перестало быть на это похоже, очень сильно», — заключил Арестович.Материал дополняется.

en.header: UAE Minister Says Crypto Will Play a "Major Role for UAE Trade Going Forward"
en.subheader: The United Arab Emirates plans to use crypto for trade in the future and also set up a working regulatory framework.
en.content: The United Arab Emirates plans to use crypto for trade in the future and also set up a working regulatory framework, according to the country's minister of state for foreign trade.Speaking with Bloomberg on Jan. 20 in Davos Switzerland, where the World Economic Forum's annual meeting is taking place, Thani Al-Zeyoudi said the UAE is considering a trade in currencies other than the US dollar. One area the country is looking to expand is cryptocurrencies, he said, adding:“Crypto will play a major role for UAE trade going forward. The most important thing is that we ensure global governance when it comes to cryptocurrencies and crypto companies."Al-Zeyoudi added that the UAE continues to work on its crypto regulatory regime. He said the focus will be on making the Gulf country a major hub with crypto-friendly policies that also have sufficient protections in place. He noted that the country has already seen some improvement in this field."We started attracting some of the companies to the country with the aim that we’ll build together the right governance and legal system, which are needed.”The comments from Al-Zeyoudi come just a day after Omar Sultan Al Olama, the UAE's minister of state for artificial intelligence, said that the nation remains committed to its goal of becoming the world’s cryptocurrency hub regardless of the recent incidents plaguing the crypto market, including the unprecedented collapse of FTX.“Them calling the UAE home is definitely a positive thing,” Olama said, hinting at cryptocurrency exchanges moving to Dubai and Abu Dhabi, in part attracted by the virtual asset regulations the UAE issued last year.Olama refuted allegations that the UAE could become a safe haven for crypto criminals. He also noted that governments should work together in order to identify and stop bad actors.“You will see them everywhere. You will see them in the Bahamas, you will see them in New York, London, and what we need to do as governments is to work together, with the industry as well, to ensure that if someone does something wrong he can't move from one place to the other,” Olama said.It is worth noting that the UAE Cabinet has recently introduced new regulation which mandates entities engaging in crypto activities to secure a license and approval from the Virtual Asset Regulatory Authority (VARA). The companies that fail to comply could face fines of up to $2.7 million.The latest regulation adds to the “Guiding Principles” for digital asset regulation and supervision that were published by the financial regulator of Abu Dhabi’s Global Market free economic zone in September.
en.summary: Minister of state for foreign trade says UAE is considering a trade in currencies.

record.subheader: UAE’s minister of state for foreign trade Thani Al-Zeyoudi noted that as the country has attracted a lot of talent from the crypto sector, the UAE now needs to roll out the correct regulation to support further growth.
record.content: UAE’s minister of state for foreign trade Thani Al-Zeyoudi noted that as the country has attracted a lot of talent from the crypto sector, the UAE now needs to roll out the correct regulation to support further growth.NewsOwn this piece of historyCollect this article as an NFTCrypto will play a “major role” in the United Arab Emirates' global trade moving forward, says the UAE’s minister of state for foreign trade Thani Al-Zeyoudi.Speaking with Bloomberg on Jan. 20 in Davos Switzerland — where world leaders are currently gathered for the 2023 World Economic Forum — Al-Zeyoudi provided a host of updates regarding the UAE’s trade partnerships and policies heading into 2023.Commenting on the crypto sector, the minister stated that “crypto will play a major role for UAE trade going forward,” as he outlined that "the most important thing is that we ensure global governance when it comes to cryptocurrencies and crypto companies.”Al-Zeyoudi went on to suggest that as the UAE works on its crypto regulatory regime, the focus will be on making the Gulf country a hub with crypto-friendly policies that also have sufficient protections in place:“We started attracting some of the companies to the country with the aim that we’ll build together the right governance and legal system, which are needed.”The comments from Al-Zeyoudi come just a week after the UAE Cabinet introduced new regulation which essentially ensures that entities engaging in crypto activities must secure a license and approval from the Virtual Asset Regulatory Authority (VARA).If companies fail to do so they will face fines of up to $2.7 million under the new law. The move adds to the “Guiding Principles” for digital asset regulation and supervision that were published by the financial regulator of Abu Dhabi’s Global Market free economic zone in September.The principles outline a friendly stance towards crypto while also pledging to comply with international standards in Anti-Money Laundering (AML), combating the financing of terrorism (CFT) and supporting financial sanctions.The UAE’s minister of state for artificial intelligence and the digital economy, Omar Sultan Al Olama also appeared at the World Economic Forum as part of a crypto-focused panel on Jan. 19.Al Olama noted that while the FTX debacle was a major concern, the UAE still wants to be a hub despite the whole ordeal.“Them [crypto companies] calling the UAE home is definitely a positive thing,” he said.The minister also distanced the UAE from assertions that its cities like Dubai tend to become key spots for disgraced crypto figures to flee to, arguing that “bad actors don’t have a nationality and don’t have a destination.”He did stress however that governments do need to work together to stop bad actors from going awol overseas.“You will see them everywhere. You will see them in the Bahamas, you will see them in New York, London, and what we need to do as governments is to work together, with the industry as well, to ensure that if someone does something wrong he can't move from one place to the other,” he said.

en.header: 60% of North Americans Invest in Crypto Without Doing Due Diligence: Study
en.subheader: 15% of North Americans don’t do any research before investing in crypto, while 49% spend less than two hours.
en.content: According to a study by Bybit and Toluna, 64% of North Americans spend less than two hours or don’t research at all before investing in cryptocurrencies.Boomers (those aged 56-64) tend to be more cautious, focusing on technical factors and inspecting the market a few days before diving into it.Jumping on the Bandwagon Without Proper AnalysisThe cryptocurrency exchange – Bybit – and the consumer intelligence platform – Toluna – surveyed over 10,000 individuals to determine whether they follow appropriate due diligence procedures prior to allocating funds in digital currencies.Nearly 50% of the North American respondents admitted becoming HODLers after evaluating the pros and cons for just a couple of hours, while 15% said they rely entirely on social media and advice from friends.Younger generations are more likely to neglect the due diligence process than the older. 33% of Gen X and 47% of Boomers spend at least a few days before investing in a cryptocurrency project.The study further revealed that over 1,700 of the participants have already bought digital assets. 50% don’t view stricter regulatory standards as a concern, while 25% would support enhanced supervision on centralized exchanges to get additional protection.Know Your Customer verification seems to have little effect on users when choosing a platform, with 50% saying they don’t have any preference on the type of requirements. On the other hand, 21% would pick a trading venue that does not impose such validation.“In an ideal world, it is understandable why some might oppose KYC verifications. However, in reality, the abuse of the system by malicious individuals needs to be prevented. Thus giving rise to the need for such forms of protection, not just for the exchanges but for the users,” the report explained.Bybit and Toluna also outlined that KYC requirements are useful tools that could prevent cybercrime and hacks, which “ultimately contribute largely to the safety and security of the ecosystem.”CEXs Are More Trusted Than BanksThe analysis showed that cryptocurrency investors have more faith in centralized exchanges than traditional banks, Internet providers, local governments, and NFTs. It is worth noting that even DeFi believers put high trust scores on CEXs.Such platforms have been in the spotlight after the collapse of FTX. Many presented proof-of-reserves to customers to display they have no liquidity issues. Despite that, a significant number of investors transferred their holdings to self-custody wallets or cashed out in the weeks after the infamous crash.The world’s leading crypto exchange – Binance – processed over $8 billion in daily withdrawals in mid-December. record.header: This Report Says Crypto Is Second Most Owned Asset By Women
record.content: Women in today’s times still do not own traditional assets due to the lack of broader adoption, but that is not the case with crypto, a report from eToro suggests. ru.content: According to a study by Bybit and Toluna, 64% of North Americans spend less than two hours or don’t research at all before investing in cryptocurrencies.Boomers (those aged 56-64) tend to be more cautious, focusing on technical factors and inspecting the market a few days before diving into it.Jumping on the Bandwagon Without Proper AnalysisThe cryptocurrency exchange – Bybit – and the consumer intelligence platform – Toluna – surveyed over 10,000 individuals to determine whether they follow appropriate due diligence procedures prior to allocating funds in digital currencies.Nearly 50% of the North American respondents admitted becoming HODLers after evaluating the pros and cons for just a couple of hours, while 15% said they rely entirely on social media and advice from friends.Younger generations are more likely to neglect the due diligence process than the older. 33% of Gen X and 47% of Boomers spend at least a few days before investing in a cryptocurrency project.The study further revealed that over 1,700 of the participants have already bought digital assets. 50% don’t view stricter regulatory standards as a concern, while 25% would support enhanced supervision on centralized exchanges to get additional protection.Know Your Customer verification seems to have little effect on users when choosing a platform, with 50% saying they don’t have any preference on the type of requirements. On the other hand, 21% would pick a trading venue that does not impose such validation.“In an ideal world, it is understandable why some might oppose KYC verifications. However, in reality, the abuse of the system by malicious individuals needs to be prevented. Thus giving rise to the need for such forms of protection, not just for the exchanges but for the users,” the report explained.Bybit and Toluna also outlined that KYC requirements are useful tools that could prevent cybercrime and hacks, which “ultimately contribute largely to the safety and security of the ecosystem.”CEXs Are More Trusted Than BanksThe analysis showed that cryptocurrency investors have more faith in centralized exchanges than traditional banks, Internet providers, local governments, and NFTs. It is worth noting that even DeFi believers put high trust scores on CEXs.Such platforms have been in the spotlight after the collapse of FTX. Many presented proof-of-reserves to customers to display they have no liquidity issues. Despite that, a significant number of investors transferred their holdings to self-custody wallets or cashed out in the weeks after the infamous crash.The world’s leading crypto exchange – Binance – processed over $8 billion in daily withdrawals in mid-December. CEO Changpeng Zhao seemed unconcerned, viewing it as a “stress test” that could show the trading venue could honor a large number of requests at any time.He argued that the withdrawal wave resulted from a FUD, saying users should feel free to store their crypto holdings in cold wallets if they have concerns. “Otherwise, we are here,” he assured.
ru.summary: Молодое поколение с большей вероятностью пренебрегает процессом должной осмотрительности.

en.header: Lithuanian author Grigory Kanovich has died in Israel
en.subheader: The Lithuanian author of books about Jews Grigory Kanovich has died in Israel.
en.content: A Soviet writer, Grigoriy Kanović, born in Lithuania, died in Israel, reported to the Israeli Embassy in the Baltic State on Twitter. "We were sad to hear of the departure of a famous Jewish writer, winner of the Lithuanian National Prize, distinguished literary, film and theatre figure, honorary chairman of EOL (the Jewish community of Lithuania. - RBK) Grigoriya Kanović," says a communication. "The Lithuanian TV channel LRT confirmed the death of his 93-year-old writer, Sergei's son. Kanović died in Tel Aviv. According to LRT, the future writer was born in Yonava, north-west Lithuania, in 1929. During the Great Patriotic War, he lived in Kazakhstan, and then the Kanovich family returned to Vilnius. He emigrated to Israel in 1993. The writer last visited Lithuania ten years ago. Kanovich wrote about the Jews of Eastern Europe, their lives in the 19th and XXth centuries. Among his famous novels was the trilogy "Sweet on the Wind," "Tears and Prayers of the Stupids," "Smile to Us, Lord." In all, he wrote more than ten novels. LRT notes that the President of Lithuania, Gitas Naused, expressed condolences on the death of Kanovich, and he called the writer "the great figure" of the country's culture one of "the most famous and loud voices in the history of Lithuanian Jews".
en.summary: Lithuanian writer, Nobel Prize winner in literature Grigory Kanovich died in Israel.

record.header: The Russian Foreign Ministry announced that the UN was distorting the facts about the implementation of the Black Sea Initiative
record.content: Moscow: On 21 January, INTERFAX.RU - Russia does not confirm the data published by the UN Secretariat on the "black Sea Initiative": 64 vessels are parked in Ukrainian ports and in inspection zones; the trans-shipment of ammonia through the "Toliatti-Odessa" pipeline was to begin as part of the implementation of the "black Sea Initiative" without additional agreements; the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Russian Federation informs the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Russian Federation. "In connection with the report to the media on the "black Sea Initiative" published by the UN Secretariat, it is in fact a matter of manipulation and reversal of the facts, which requires the provision of real data and assessments by Russia as a party (unlike the United Nations) to the two agreements concluded in Istanbul on 22 July 2022," the report published on Saturday on the website of the Russian foreign policy office. On Smolen Square, 668 vessels with 18,224,860 tons of food on board were said to have left the ports of Odessa, Black Sea and South (as of 20 January) as part of the Black Sea Initiative. "In the cargo range, 46.1 per cent is occupied by feed corn, 5.9 per cent by shroth, 5.5 per cent by rape and other animal feed crops, the proportion of wheat is only 27.57 per cent, but it is emphasized in the United Nations bulletin. "The clear aim is to provide "right" humanitarian figures on recipients of "emerging economies" (a total of 64 per cent) for some reason to include States such as Israel, South Korea and the Gulf monarchies, which are clearly not experiencing difficulties in the development of the economy or food security", the report states. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs added that "the real geography of Ukrainian food recipients is as follows: high-income countries (EU, Great Britain, etc.) received 8.6 million tons of cargo (47 per cent), higher-middle income (China, Jordan, Malaysia, etc.) 6.1 million tons (33 per cent), lower-middle-income countries (Bangladesh, India, Indonesia, Pakistan, etc.) 2.9 million tons (16 per cent). Only 551,527 tons (3 per cent) were sent to countries in need (Somalia, Ethiopia, the Sudan, Yemen, Afghanistan and Djibouti), including 396,169 tons (2 per cent) by vessels chartered by WFP." The Russian foreign policy department added: "It is noteworthy that the share of these States in general statistics is declining - almost 4 per cent in the first 120 days of the initiative, now 3 per cent. It should be noted that it is for this reason that the United Nations quickly reclassified the "black Sea Initiative" from humanitarian to commercial and refused to publish information on the recipients of cargo under the pretext of commercial secrecy." "There is also no evidence from the United Nations press release that more than 100 vessels are located in Turkish territorial waters and connected to the initiative, as well as an average waiting time of 21 days. At present, 64 vessels are parked in Ukrainian ports and inspection zones, the list of priorities for their checks and passage is drawn up by the Ukrainian side, and the Russian representatives have no influence over it," stated to the Ministry. "At the same time, attention has been drawn on several occasions to the problem of artificial accumulation of dry cargo in the port of Istanbul, which is being created by Ukrainian traders chartering vessels without taking into account agreed rules and the timing of registration and participation in the initiative," is noted on Smallen Square. In the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Russian Federation stressed that "until such vessels are included in the initiative, they cannot be considered participants and the Joint Coordination Centre in Istanbul is not responsible for them". The Ministry added that the United Nations communication specifically referred to the task of resuming the export of ammonia from the port of the South as set out in the Black Sea Initiative. "Despite the fact that such removal of fertilizers, including ammonia, should have started at the same time as the transport of Ukrainian food, the document vaguely reported some discussions between certain parties with a view to reaching an agreement", added there. "Russian position on this matter has been repeatedly and in detail communicated to the United Nations - the trans-shipment of ammonia should have started as part of the implementation of the "black Sea Initiative." No additional arrangements should be required in this regard. The technical possibilities for resuscitating the pipeline are available. Just as the willingness of the companies servicing it has been expressed by the Russian agency." "Only and exclusively, Kiev's consent is lacking, blocking the supply of fertilizer raw materials (sufficient to provide food to 200 million people), leaving them with a set of political preconditions from the release of prisoners of war to assistance in the sale of stolen goods. The United Nations, which is actively calling for the expansion of Ukrainian grain exports, is not working specifically on this issue. They're referring to some kind of negotiation. It is not clear, the truth is, between whom and what, since Russian representatives are not involved in any such contacts," the report says. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs ' fertilisers ' exports stressed that "at the very end of the UN ' s information sheet, literally in one paragraph, reference is made to the second document, signed in Istanbul on 22 July 2022, on the normalization of Russian exports of agricultural products and fertilizers". "It is silent, however, that both arrangements are integral parts of the same "package" proposed by Antonio Guterrish and should be implemented in conjunction with each other," was added at the Ministry. The Russian Federation considers that the implementation of Moscow's proposal for the donation of 262,000 tons of fertilizer to the poorest countries to be particularly indicative in this regard. "The official appeal to the UN Secretary of State on 7 September 2022, provided all the necessary information and information," was added. "The first and only shipment of 20,000 tons of produce was sent from the Netherlands to Malawi on 28 November 2022. The Russian side further assumed all the costs of delivering and transporting the goods, as well as paying the "intermediation services" of the UN/WFP in the amount of $200,000. "Even though it is a humanitarian operation and assistance to those in need in the run-up to the new planting season," the report states. "The revenues to the port of Mozambique on 28 December 2022 and must now be on the way to Malawi. Thus, it took almost five months for only one and a small portion of the United Nations-sponsored fertilizer to be shipped and the cargo had not yet reached the recipient," was added to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Russian Federation. In Smolen Square, it is believed that "if the implementation of this purely humanitarian initiative is progressing so hard and twirling, we clearly do not have to talk about normalizing our exports of agricultural products and fertilizers with the help of the United Nations".

ru.header: В Израиле умер литовский автор Григорий Канович
ru.subheader: В Израиле умер литовский автор книг о евреях Григорий Канович
ru.content: Советский писатель Григорий Канович, родившийся в Литве, умер в Израиле, сообщило посольство Израиля в балтийском государстве в своем Twitter.«Мы были опечалены известием об уходе из жизни известного еврейского писателя, лауреата Литовской национальной премии, выдающегося деятеля литературы, кино и театра, почетного председателя ЕОЛ (Еврейская община Литвы. — РБК) Григория Кановича», — сказано в сообщении.Литовскому телеканалу LRT информацию о смерти 93-летнего писателя подтвердил его сын Сергей. Канович скончался в Тель-Авиве.Как указывает LRT, будущий писатель родился в городе Йонава на северо-западе Литвы в 1929 году. Во время Великой Отечественной войны жил в Казахстане, а потом семья Кановича вернулась в Вильнюс. В Израиль он эмигрировал в 1993 году. Литву писатель последний раз посетил десять лет назад.Канович писал о евреях Восточной Европы, их жизни в XIX—XX веках. Среди его известных романов — трилогия «Свечи на ветру», дилогия «Слезы и молитвы дураков», «Улыбнись нам, Господи». Всего он написал более десяти романов.LRT отмечает, что соболезнования в связи со смертью Кановича выразил президент Литвы Гитанас Науседа. Он назвал писателя «великим деятелем» культуры страны, одним из «самых известных и громких голосов в истории литовских евреев».
ru.summary: Литовский писатель, лауреат Нобелевской премии по литературе Григорий Канович скончался в Израиле.

en.header: The Taliban announced their readiness to create special forces to protect the TAPI gas pipeline project
en.content: Moscow. On 21 January, INTERFAX.RU, the Taliban Movement in control of Afghanistan (the Russian terrorist organization) stated that it was prepared to create a special force to ensure the security of the TAPI transnational gas pipeline project (Turkmenistan - Afghanistan - Pakistan - India). "With the re-establishment of the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan (the Taliban - IF Government) in the country, full security has been ensured, which gives more scope for the project now than ever before," states the statement of the Deputy Prime Minister of the Government of the Taliban on economic issues. "The Islamic Emirates is prepared, if necessary, to form a special force to protect the project. The Islamic Emirates of Afghanistan views the reconstruction of the country and the revitalization of its economic infrastructure as its responsibility and considers that the political, security and economic prosperity of the region is the shared responsibility of the Member States," the statement states. The official statement on economic issues on TAPI and other national projects, published on Saturday evening, states that "a significant economic project at the regional level was initiated during the first Taliban rule in Afghanistan (1996-2001). ), "but the American occupation of Afghanistan caused a delay in its completion." On Tuesday, 17 January, the Director General of TAPI - Pipeline Company Limited (TCL) Muhammad Amanov, headed by the delegation of Turkmenistan, met in Kabul with the leadership of the power unit of the movement: representatives of the Ministry of Internal Affairs, the Ministry of Defence and the General Intelligence Department of the Taliban. "The Director of the Public Protection Department of the Ministry of the Interior, Mawlawi Hamas, in his statement, assured that the TAPI project was vital to the Afghan people and that the Islamic Emirates would do its utmost to ensure their safety," reported the Taliban Ministry of Internal Affairs press centre. The TAPI project (Turkmenistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan-India) involves the construction of a transnational gas pipeline through four countries, with a gas pipeline of 33 billion cubic metres per year from the Galkinish Turkmen field through the Afghan cities of Herat and Kandahar, the Pakistani Quetta and Multan to the town of Fazilka in western India, with a total length of 1,814 km, 207 km for Turkmenistan, 774 km for Afghanistan and 826 km for Pakistan to the border with India.
en.summary: The controlling Afghan Taliban movement (banned in Russia) announced its readiness to create special units to ensure the security of the TAPI gas pipeline.

ru.header: Талибы заявили о готовности создать специальные силы для защиты проекта газопровода ТАПИ
ru.content: Москва. 21 января. INTERFAX.RU - Контролирующее Афганистан движение "Талибан" (запрещенная в России террористическая организация) заявило, что готово создать специальные силы для обеспечения безопасности транснационального проекта газопровода ТАПИ (Туркменистан - Афганистан - Пакистан - Индия)."С восстановлением Исламского Эмирата Афганистана (правительство талибов - ИФ) в стране была обеспечена полная безопасность, что дает больше возможностей для реализации этого проекта сейчас, чем когда-либо прежде", - говорится в заявлении аппарата вице-премьера правительства талибов по экономическим вопросам."В случае необходимости Исламский Эмират готов сформировать специальную силу для защиты проекта. Исламский Эмират Афганистан рассматривает восстановление страны и оживление ее экономической инфраструктуры как свою обязанность и считает, что политическое, безопасное и экономическое процветание региона является общей ответственностью государств-членов", - говорится в заявлении.В официальном заявлении по экономическим вопросам относительно ТАПИ и других национальных проектов, опубликованном в субботу вечером, говорится, что "значительный экономический проект на региональном уровне был инициирован еще во время первого правления талибов в Афганистане (1996-2001 гг.), "но американская оккупация Афганистана вызвала задержку в его завершении".Во вторник, 17 января, генеральный директор ТАПИ - Pipeline Company Limited (TPCL) Мухамметмырат Аманов во главе делегации Туркменистана встретился в Кабуле с руководством силового блока движения: представителями МВД, Минобороны и Главного управления разведки талибов."Директор Департамента общественной защиты Министерства внутренних дел мавлави Хамас в своем выступлении заверил, что проект ТАПИ является жизненно важным для афганского народа и что Исламский Эмират сделает все возможное для обеспечения его безопасности", - сообщил пресс-центр МВД талибов.Проект ТАПИ (Туркменистан-Афганистан-Пакистан-Индия) предусматривает строительство транснационального газопровода, проходящего через четыре страны. Газопровод мощностью 33 млрд кубометров газа в год пройдет от туркменского месторождения "Галкыныш" через афганские города Герат и Кандагар, пакистанские Кветту и Мултан до города Фазилка на западе Индии. Общая протяженность газопровода - 1 814 км, из них 207 км - по территории Туркменистана, 774 км - Афганистана и 826 км - по территории Пакистана до границы с Индией.
ru.summary: Контролирующее афганское движение «Талибан» (запрещена в России) заявило о готовности создать специальные подразделения для обеспечения безопасности газопровода ТАПИ.

record.content: Moscow: On 21 January, INTERFAX.RU - Russia does not confirm the data published by the UN Secretariat on the "black Sea Initiative": 64 vessels are parked in Ukrainian ports and in inspection zones; the trans-shipment of ammonia through the "Toliatti-Odessa" pipeline was to begin as part of the implementation of the "black Sea Initiative" without additional agreements; the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Russian Federation informs the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Russian Federation. "In connection with the report to the media on the "black Sea Initiative" published by the UN Secretariat, it is in fact a matter of manipulation and reversal of the facts, which requires the provision of real data and assessments by Russia as a party (unlike the United Nations) to the two agreements concluded in Istanbul on 22 July 2022," the report published on Saturday on the website of the Russian foreign policy office. On Smolen Square, 668 vessels with 18,224,860 tons of food on board were said to have left the ports of Odessa, Black Sea and South (as of 20 January) as part of the Black Sea Initiative. "In the cargo range, 46.1 per cent is occupied by feed corn, 5.9 per cent by shroth, 5.5 per cent by rape and other animal feed crops, the proportion of wheat is only 27.57 per cent, but it is emphasized in the United Nations bulletin. "The clear aim is to provide "right" humanitarian figures on recipients of "emerging economies" (a total of 64 per cent) for some reason to include States such as Israel, South Korea and the Gulf monarchies, which are clearly not experiencing difficulties in the development of the economy or food security", the report states. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs added that "the real geography of Ukrainian food recipients is as follows: high-income countries (EU, Great Britain, etc.) received 8.6 million tons of cargo (47 per cent), higher-middle income (China, Jordan, Malaysia, etc.) 6.1 million tons (33 per cent), lower-middle-income countries (Bangladesh, India, Indonesia, Pakistan, etc.) 2.9 million tons (16 per cent). Only 551,527 tons (3 per cent) were sent to countries in need (Somalia, Ethiopia, the Sudan, Yemen, Afghanistan and Djibouti), including 396,169 tons (2 per cent) by vessels chartered by WFP." The Russian foreign policy department added: "It is noteworthy that the share of these States in general statistics is declining - almost 4 per cent in the first 120 days of the initiative, now 3 per cent. It should be noted that it is for this reason that the United Nations quickly reclassified the "black Sea Initiative" from humanitarian to commercial and refused to publish information on the recipients of cargo under the pretext of commercial secrecy." "There is also no evidence from the United Nations press release that more than 100 vessels are located in Turkish territorial waters and connected to the initiative, as well as an average waiting time of 21 days. At present, 64 vessels are parked in Ukrainian ports and inspection zones, the list of priorities for their checks and passage is drawn up by the Ukrainian side, and the Russian representatives have no influence over it," stated to the Ministry. "At the same time, attention has been drawn on several occasions to the problem of artificial accumulation of dry cargo in the port of Istanbul, which is being created by Ukrainian traders chartering vessels without taking into account agreed rules and the timing of registration and participation in the initiative," is noted on Smallen Square. In the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, the Russian Federation stressed that "until such vessels are included in the initiative, they cannot be considered participants and the Joint Coordination Centre in Istanbul is not responsible for them". The Ministry added that the United Nations communication specifically referred to the task of resuming the export of ammonia from the port of the South as set out in the Black Sea Initiative. "Despite the fact that such removal of fertilizers, including ammonia, should have started at the same time as the transport of Ukrainian food, the document vaguely reported some discussions between certain parties with a view to reaching an agreement", added there. "Russian position on this matter has been repeatedly and in detail communicated to the United Nations - the trans-shipment of ammonia should have started as part of the implementation of the "black Sea Initiative." No additional arrangements should be required in this regard. The technical possibilities for resuscitating the pipeline are available. Just as the willingness of the companies servicing it has been expressed by the Russian agency." "Only and exclusively, Kiev's consent is lacking, blocking the supply of fertilizer raw materials (sufficient to provide food to 200 million people), leaving them with a set of political preconditions from the release of prisoners of war to assistance in the sale of stolen goods. The United Nations, which is actively calling for the expansion of Ukrainian grain exports, is not working specifically on this issue. They're referring to some kind of negotiation. It is not clear, the truth is, between whom and what, since Russian representatives are not involved in any such contacts," the report says. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs ' fertilisers ' exports stressed that "at the very end of the UN ' s information sheet, literally in one paragraph, reference is made to the second document, signed in Istanbul on 22 July 2022, on the normalization of Russian exports of agricultural products and fertilizers". "It is silent, however, that both arrangements are integral parts of the same "package" proposed by Antonio Guterrish and should be implemented in conjunction with each other," was added at the Ministry. The Russian Federation considers that the implementation of Moscow's proposal for the donation of 262,000 tons of fertilizer to the poorest countries to be particularly indicative in this regard. "The official appeal to the UN Secretary of State on 7 September 2022, provided all the necessary information and information," was added. "The first and only shipment of 20,000 tons of produce was sent from the Netherlands to Malawi on 28 November 2022. The Russian side further assumed all the costs of delivering and transporting the goods, as well as paying the "intermediation services" of the UN/WFP in the amount of $200,000. "Even though it is a humanitarian operation and assistance to those in need in the run-up to the new planting season," the report states. "The revenues to the port of Mozambique on 28 December 2022 and must now be on the way to Malawi. Thus, it took almost five months for only one and a small portion of the United Nations-sponsored fertilizer to be shipped and the cargo had not yet reached the recipient," was added to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Russian Federation. In Smolen Square, it is believed that "if the implementation of this purely humanitarian initiative is progressing so hard and twirling, we clearly do not have to talk about normalizing our exports of agricultural products and fertilizers with the help of the United Nations".

en.header: US Government Seizes $700 Million in Assets From Disgraced FTX Co-Founder Sam Bankman-Fried
en.subheader: Court filings detailed that the U.S. government seized a series of bank accounts belonging to Bankman-Fried, holding millions in cash.
en.content: Federal prosecutors have seized $697 million in assets, mostly comprised of more than 56 million Robinhood shares worth $526 million, from FTX co-founder Sam Bankman-Fried. Court filings detailed that the U.S. government seized a series of bank accounts belonging to Bankman-Fried, holding millions in cash.US Government Seizes Millions in Cash and Robinhood Shares From FTX Co-Founder; SBF Denies Misappropriation of Customer AssetsThe U.S. government has seized nearly $700 million from the former FTX CEO and co-founder, Sam Bankman-Fried (SBF), according to court documents reviewed by CNBC. Most of the funds came from the 56,273,269 shares of Robinhood Markets Inc. (Nasdaq: HOOD) owned by Bankman-Fried. Using exchange rates from Jan. 20, 2023, the Hood shares are worth more than $526 million.Furthermore, CNBC reporters Rohan Goswami and MacKenzie Sigalos detail that nearly $56 million held in four bank accounts was seized as well. Three accounts holding $6 million were allegedly held at Silvergate Bank and one account reportedly held at Moonstone Bank held $50 million. In total, $171 million in cash was taken by the federal government from Bankman-Fried. Moonstone Bank explained on Jan. 19, 2023, that the financial institution will officially be exiting the crypto space.Alameda Research invested $11.5 million into Moonstone Bank, also known as Farmington State Bank, through FBH, Moonstone’s holding company. Federal prosecutors believe the $697 million in assets, mostly made up of Robinhood shares, were acquired using funds stolen from FTX customers. Bankman-Fried maintains his innocence and has “denied misappropriating customer assets,” Sigalos explained on Friday.Additionally, federal agents also seized funds that belonged to SBF that were held on the crypto exchanges Binance and Binance US. The U.S. government revealed intentions to seize the Robinhood shares during the first week of January 2023, and the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) initiated the process.Bankman-Fried attempted to regain access to the shares, noting that he needed the money to pay for legal expenses. The U.S. government can seize funds from citizens suspected of wrongdoing without necessarily charging them with a crime and from charged suspects awaiting trial. Federal prosecutors do not believe the assets seized are the property in the bankruptcy estate.

record.header: FED Make Major Move: $700 Million Seized from Sam Bankman Fried
record.content: The United States Federal authorities have seized $697 million from Sam Bankman Fried, Founder of cryptocurrency exchange FTX. The majority of the assets were being in the form of shares of the popular trading app, Robinhood. SBF had previously announced that he had acquired a 7.6% stake in Robinhood stating that it was an attractive investment opportunity.These Robinhood shares which are worth $50 million have been claimed by Sam, BlockFi representatives, and the leadership of FTX Debtors. Federal authorities have alleged that these shares were acquired using the funds that were stolen from FTX customers.Even though the reason for the seizure has not been made public yet, it has raised questions about the legality of such actions and their implication in the cryptocurrency industry. Several experts are concerned that the future of the crypto industry will be packed with stringent regulations.The United States government stated that over $6 million from three accounts at Silvergate Bank were under the name of FTX Digital Markets. These assets were initially owned by a Bahamian company and were later acquired by the US government on Jan 11.Silvergate Bank reported a loss of $1 billion in the fourth quarter of 2022 after FTX’s collapse. Moreover, around $50 million was stored at Moonstone Bank, a financial institution in the U.S. that has connections to the administration of FTX.The case is still going on and the outcomes will have a deep impact on the crypto industry.

en.header: The UK opened a case after the discovery of body fragments in a bathhouse near St. Petersburg
en.subheader: SK: after the discovery of body fragments in a bathhouse near St. Petersburg, a criminal case was opened
en.content: In Leningrad province, criminal proceedings were initiated under article 105, paragraph 1, of the Criminal Code, following the discovery of body fragments in Allwolzhsk, as reported on the website of the UK Regional Investigation Department. "On January 21, 2023, in a bathhouse located in a private house in the city of All Volgozhsk in Leningrad province, severed body fragments were found in four bags", says the communication. Article 105 of the Criminal Code provides for up to 15 years of imprisonment. According to 47news, a citizen of Allvolzhska named Arkady called his friend Julia and asked him to help "save a corpse." The woman then went to the police and the police went to the house on the street of Necrasova, where they found bags of body fragments. In November, a man was detained in Petersburg, Kolpin district in the Izhora River, where a sports bag with body parts was found. The UK also initiated a criminal investigation. "Fontanca" wrote that the bag contained fragments of women's legs and a piece of asphalt, parts of the body were in the water at that time between 9 and 13 days.
en.summary: Investigators have opened a criminal case into the discovery of body fragments in a bathhouse near St. Petersburg after they were found in a bathhouse located in the village of Vsevolozhsky, Vsevolozhsky district, Leningrad region.

record.header: The trial of the attempted murder of two teenagers begins in Moscow
record.content: Moscow. On 20 January, INTERFAX.RU, the Kuzminsk Court of Moscow, will commence criminal proceedings in late January on the attempted murder of two underage girls born in 2006 and 2004, informed Interfax at Mosgorsud Press Service. "Preliminary criminal proceedings against Nikita Lebedev are scheduled to take place on 24 January and will take place in closed session", said the court's representative, according to the investigation, Lebedev, using the false names of pages on the social network VKontakte during 2020, met minors who were offered to perform life- and health-threatening tricks at high altitude, record them in a photo or video camera and send them as proof of a request. For example, he encouraged minor victims to hang themselves upside down from windows and roofs of houses, which posed a real threat to their lives, and it was only by chance that there were no victims, according to the UK that "the actions of the Lebedovs were committed because of his sexual preference disorder." The Zbedev was charged with attempted murder (art. 30, para. 3, para. 2 (a), of art. 105, of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation).

ru.header: СК завел дело после обнаружения фрагментов тела в бане под Петербургом
ru.subheader: СК: после обнаружения фрагментов тела в бане под Петербургом возбуждено уголовное дело
ru.content: В Ленинградской области возбуждено уголовное дело по статье об убийстве (ч. 1 ст. 105 УК) после обнаружения во Всеволжске фрагментов тела, сообщается на сайте Следственного управления СК по региону.«21 января 2023 года в бане, расположенной на территории частного дома в городе Всеволожск Ленинградской области, обнаружены отчлененные фрагменты тела в четырех пакетах», — сказано в сообщении.Статья 105 УК предусматривает до 15 лет лишения свободы.Как сообщает 47news, житель Всеволжска по имени Аркадий позвонил своей знакомой Юлии и попросил помочь ему «спрятать труп». Женщина после этого обратилась в полицию, и полицейские направились к дому по улице Некрасова, где и нашли пакеты с фрагментами тела. Мужчину задержали.В ноябре в Петербурге, в Колпинском районе в реке Ижора нашли спортивную сумку с частями тела. СК также возбудил уголовное дело. «Фонтанка» писала, что в сумке были фрагменты женских ног и кусок асфальта, части тела находились в воде к тому моменту от 9 до 13 дней.
ru.summary: Следователи возбудили уголовное дело по факту обнаружения фрагментов тел в бане под Санкт-Петербургом после того, как они были обнаружены в бане, расположенной в поселке Всеволожский Всеволожского района Ленинградской области.
