en.header: This Report Says Crypto Is Second Most Owned Asset By Women
en.content: Women in today’s times still do not own traditional assets due to the lack of broader adoption, but that is not the case with crypto, a report from eToro suggests. The report titled “Retail Investor Beat” showed that cryptocurrencies happen to be the second most owned asset by women after fiat currency or cash.Crypto undoubtedly had its worst year in 2022, with the overall global ownership increasing from just 36% to 39% in a quarter, despite that, the adoption of this particular asset class grew substantially among women.The report shows that women’s ownership of digital assets rose from 29% in the third quarter of 2022 to 34% in the last quarter of 2022. This implies that somewhere, investing in cryptocurrencies has made more sense to women than investing in or possessing traditional financial assets.The report was published after the eToro team surveyed close to 10,000 global retail investors in 13 different countries. The survey also concentrated on the finding that women are more likely to hold cryptocurrency.On the contrary, men have barely increased their crypto ownership compared to women, as male ownership witnessed a 1% increase in the aforementioned time period.What Could Be The Reason Behind Increased Female Crypto OwnershipWomen’s increasing digital asset ownership simply demonstrates that traditional financial markets have failed to be more inclusive of women. For those who are interested in investing in crypto, the main reason is to achieve higher returns in a shorter span of time.Some have also shown faith and belief in the power of blockchain, as crypto could have the power to act as a transformative asset class in the future. And for those who have eschewed investing in crypto, their biggest fear behind this decision is because of the perceived risks and volatility that are attached to the industry.Some have also stated that regulatory ambiguity has kept them away from investing in the asset class. This could merely mean that women are more risk-takers because they have invested in this asset class despite the industry’s risks and uncertainties.Other Populations Who Are Interested In BlockchainThe data also discloses that along with women who are risk-takers and have been pro-digital assets, older investors have also shown keen interest in buying the dip.The report suggests that retail investors holding crypto between the ages of 35 and 44 and 45 and 54 have shown an increase of 5%,  which shows that the older population has been accumulating this asset class.In regards to businesses, apart from retail investors, many businesses have already started to take crypto investments seriously. Another recent report published by the blockchain company CasperLabs in partnership with Zogby Analytics reflected an interest in using blockchain by businesses specifically.The survey of over 600 corporate decision-makers in the United States, the United Kingdom, and China showed that businesses are beginning to invest in blockchain technology, in addition to retail investors who already do so.87% of these organizations said they planned to invest in blockchain technology in the next year. And among the nations that were surveyed, the findings were inclined towards China, with more than half the respondents showing interest in investing in blockchain.
en.summary: Crypto is the second most owned asset by women after fiat currency or cash. The report was published after the eToro team surveyed close to 10,000 global retail investors in 13 different countries. On the contrary, men have barely increased their crypto ownership compared to women.

record.header: Today in Crypto: Car Crashed Into Sam Bankman-Fried's House Barricade, Ransomware Payments Fell 40% in 2022, Crypto Became the Second Most Widely Owned Asset Class for Women
record.subheader: Get your daily, bite-sized digest of cryptoasset and blockchain-related news – investigating the stories flying under the radar of today's crypto news.
record.content: Crime newsA car "recently" intentionally rammed into a metal barricade outside the California, USA, home where FTX founder Sam Bankman-Fried is serving out his house arrest, the New York Post reported, citing the former CEO’s lawyers. Allegedly, three men exited the car and told a security guard: “You won’t be able to keep us out,” the attorneys claimed in a Manhattan federal court filing on Thursday.Ransomware payments are down 40%, with attackers extorting at least $456.8 million in funds in 2022, compared to $765.6 million in 2021, according to a new report by blockchain forensics firm Chainalysis. "That doesn't mean attacks are down, or at least not as much as the drastic dropoff in payments would suggest," it said. "Instead, we believe that much of the decline is due to victim organizations increasingly refusing to pay ransomware attackers."Crypto is now the second most widely owned asset class for women after cash, “suggesting it is succeeding where traditional financial markets have sometimes failed in bringing more women to the table,” said an eToro report. The female ownership of crypto jumped from 29% in Q3 to 34% in Q4 2022, whilst men saw only a 1 percentage point rise from 42% to 43% of the surveyed investors.Global offshore law firm Harneys acted as Cayman Islands counsel to HashKey Capital, a global asset manager specializing in blockchain and crypto, on the successful $500 million closing of its third fund, HashKey FinTech Investment Fund III, said a press release. The “new fund will further advance crypto and blockchain initiatives worldwide, with a focus on emerging markets,” it added.Xclaim, an independent trading platform for cryptoassets locked by bankruptcy, announced that thousands of customers of several bankrupt crypto exchanges, including FTX, BlockFi, Celsius, and Voyager, have listed their accounts for sale, representing more than $200 million of cryptoassets. Xclaim enables crypto account holders to recover the market value of accounts that are inaccessible during the pendency of a bankruptcy, said the press release.Bitcoin miner CleanSpark announced a nearly $16 million expansion, with projected completion in late spring, holding up to 16,000 miners. Per the press release, it started construction on the second phase of one of its newest sites in Washington, Georgia, USA, consisting of Antminer S19j Pro and Antminer S19 XP machines. Upon completion, the new phase will add up to 2.2 exahashes per second (EH/s) of computing power to the company’s mining capacity.Layer 1 blockchain Fantom launched a decentralized funding mechanism to finance blockchain projects through a community-driven governance process. The so-called Ecosystem Vault is an on-chain fund financed by 10% of the transaction fees on Fantom and controlled by the community, providing an opportunity for projects to secure funding in their efforts to build decentralized apps (dapps) on the blockchain, a blog post said.AllianceBlock, which builds gateways between traditional finance (TradFi) and decentralized finance (DeFi) through decentralized and trustless infrastructure, announced a strategic partnership with ARTBANX, a customizable and secure collection management system for collectors, art professionals, and financial institutions. Per a press release, this partnership is a first of its kind. ARTBANX enables art to become a bankable asset class, which will be expanded with a marketplace built on blockchain technology. AllianceBlock, with Nexera Protocol’s infrastructure and NexeraID’s identity management toolkit, will allow the tokenization of physical artworks and facilitate a marketplace for art, it said.Blockchain technology company Native announced the launch of its project-owned decentralized exchange (DEX) layer for crypto. Per the press release, “Native created this technology because the crypto ecosystem has become too reliant on exchanges and market makers.” This technology enables any project to become its own DEX, they added.

en.header: The trial of the attempted murder of two teenagers begins in Moscow
en.content: Moscow. On 20 January, INTERFAX.RU, the Kuzminsk Court of Moscow, will commence criminal proceedings in late January on the attempted murder of two underage girls born in 2006 and 2004, informed Interfax at Mosgorsud Press Service. "Preliminary criminal proceedings against Nikita Lebedev are scheduled to take place on 24 January and will take place in closed session", said the court's representative, according to the investigation, Lebedev, using the false names of pages on the social network VKontakte during 2020, met minors who were offered to perform life- and health-threatening tricks at high altitude, record them in a photo or video camera and send them as proof of a request. For example, he encouraged minor victims to hang themselves upside down from windows and roofs of houses, which posed a real threat to their lives, and it was only by chance that there were no victims, according to the UK that "the actions of the Lebedovs were committed because of his sexual preference disorder." The Zbedev was charged with attempted murder (art. 30, para. 3, para. 2 (a), of art. 105, of the Criminal Code of the Russian Federation).
en.summary: The Moscow City Court has begun considering the merits of the case of the murder of two young girls born in 2006 and 2004, committed by a group of people by prior agreement.

record.header: Zadornov presented arguments against the merger of Otkritie Bank with VTB
record.subheader: The head of Otkritie, Mikhail Zadornov, in a letter to the Ministry of Finance, called the advantages of joining the bank to VTB controversial and listed the disadvantages of the transaction under discussion. In his opinion, despite the sanctions, Otkritie can still be sold to investors.
record.content: Michael Zadornov, the head of the Open, in a letter to the Ministry of Finance, described the benefits of the bank's accession to the VTB as controversial and listed the disadvantages of the transaction under discussion. In his view, despite the sanctions, the Open could still be sold to investors Michael Zadornov The Open Bank's open-up deal will not achieve the objectives of increasing the capital sustainability and efficiency of the banking sector, and has "a few significant disadvantages." This is stated in Michael Zadornov's letter to the Minister of Finance, Anton Siluanov, the text of which is available to RBC and confirmed the source in the financial market. "We are not familiar with this letter. The decision is being taken by the President. The decision is under way," reported WTB to RBC. The Government's press service sent a request to the Ministry of Finance. The Ministry's spokesman noted that the issue of bank integration was being addressed "in accordance with the President's instructions." The CEC did not respond to the RBC's request. How did the "Open" decide not to sell, but to join the WTB Bank "Open" in 2017 as a result of sedation. After financial recovery, the regulator announced its intention to sell the asset in 2021, but the deal had to be postponed because of the coronavirus pandemic. In the summer of last year, the BEC again announced the start of pre-market preparations for "Open" with two scenarios being considered: the sale of 50 per cent plus one to a strategic investor, or the initial placement of a share in a bank on the stock exchange (IPO). At the end of 2021, Zadornov stated that the applicants at the "Open" were on February 24, 2022, Russia had launched a military operation in Ukraine, and on the same day, the "Open" bank was under United States block sanctions. At the end of April, it was known that the head of the BTB, Andrei Costin, had invited the Government to join its bank (also under U.S. block sanctions) "Open" and the Crimean RNSB. This would save on the costs of specific banks, as well as reduce the cost of the budget "to stabilize the banking sector" in the context of the crisis, writing "Commersant" at the end of April. According to the publication, the idea was endorsed by President Vladimir Putin. The head of the CEC, Elvira Nabiullina, supported the consolidation in public. "We do not see the possibility of selling the Open Bank to the market in the foreseeable future either," she explained. The letter from Zadornov provides both financial and legal arguments against the transaction. Openness's accession to the VTB will not significantly improve the latter's performance or guarantee greater operational efficiency of the business, I think Zadonnov. The Openup estimates that its own capital will not result in a tangible increase in the adequacy of the combined bank's capital (maximum +0.4 p.). (c) The right to freedom of opinion and expression (art. to standard H1.0. According to the annex to the letter, as at 1 February, the regulatory capital of WTB was 1.7 trillion roubles. and the ratio of self-sufficiency H1.0 to 10.2 per cent (this is below the required level of 11.5 per cent, but for banking groups the standard of H20.0, calculated differently, is used. On the same date, the Open figures were 368.7 billion roubles and 13 per cent. This means that the standard of capital adequacy of the combined bank would be only 10.6 per cent. The Openship Manual states that the past experience of the WTB in consolidating the subsidiary retail bank, VTB24, failed to produce the desired effect. "The declared synergy from the unification of banks between 2018 and 2019 was not confirmed in practice — total expenditure, on the other hand, increased sharply," the letter states. Prior to the transition to the Open, Zadornov led the WTB24: at the end of 2017, after 12 years of work at the bank, he resigned early due to the accession of the "dog" to the VTB, and in January 2018, he headed the "Open". There are legal risks of integration with the VTB. The State Bank was the stockholder of the "Open" with a 7% share prior to its disposition, and the bankruptcy law "has an explicit ban on the owners of more than 1% of the shares of the banked banks to participate in their subsequent acquisition" is stated in the letter. The circumvention of the bankruptcy law by some legislative changes, in the view of Revelation, sets a negative precedent and "transmitting to the market, the ex-owner acquires a fiscally held asset", indicates Zadronov. In addition, the Revelations believe that the VTB "will not be motivated to complete the trials" against the former owners of the Revelation, Binbank and Rosgostrah. Once the CEC has been cleared, as the new owner of the asset, the court tries to recover the funds withdrawn from the bank. With it, the "Trust" non-core asset bank is running a process to which problematic assets have been transferred from the balance sheet of banked private banks. The BC, as a shareholder, will incur potential losses in the transfer of an asset to the VTB. Bank management refers to the independent evaluator's calculations made at the end of 2021, according to which the capital of the "Open" was 487 billion roubles. Since then, market conditions have changed and market multipliers of the largest banks have been adjusted, so the realization of "Open" shares at a price determined by the evaluator "will result in a loss on the balance sheet of the Bank of Russia and the inability to return funds to the Russian Federation in the short term", notes the author of the letter. The BC's cost of the opening and Binbank sanitation was estimated at more than 2 trillion rubles. The consolidation of the two major banks "does not meet the challenge of enhancing the capital sustainability of the banking sector". The letter states that it is difficult to assess the extent of possible pre-capitalization that banks may require against the background of crisis and sanctions — for example, there is no understanding of what losses players will record from the write-off of assets abroad. The BC had previously estimated the potential pre-capitalization volume of 2.5 to 3 trillion roubles. , indicates the Zadrons. On 18 May, the Deputy Minister of Finance, Alexei Moses, told journalists that it would not be possible to calculate the costs of bank support before the fourth quarter. The deal, he said, will be closed as early as this year. As noted in the letter, when deciding to precapitalize a separate bank, it is necessary to present a "target market picture" for the medium and long term, and now there is a possibility of expanding the sanctions against banks. What "Open" Bank has approached the crisis and consolidated IFRS reporting, "Open" has shown profits since 2018. As at 1 February 2022, its loan portfolio was over 2.6 trillion roubles. 77.6 per cent of this amount is for corporate loans. The "Open" deposit base was estimated at 2.6 trillion roubles. Just over 1 trillion roubles. This is public deposits. The size of the BTB loan portfolio is about five times the size of the "Open" portfolio and the amount of funds raised was 6.4 times the amount. According to the letter, in 2022, Open will receive up to 30 billion rubles of loss, but no pre-capitalization will be required: losses will be absorbed without violating the standards. In 2019-2021, the bank updated the IT infrastructure to take account of import substitution and generally does not experience difficulties in operating independently. If the two banks combine an increase in the adequacy of their own funds, H1.0 will only be 0.4 p.p., while the adequacy of capital capital H1.1 will be 0.8 p.p., unless there are additional capital injections or asset optimizations, the Managing Director of the Approval Unit, Yuri Belikov, estimates. "This increase in standards does not indeed provide a great potential for income-generating asset growth, does not significantly increase the absorption buffer, and can be quickly disposed of in practice," says the analyst. The scale of the impact of the Open-up would be irrelevant to the capital of the VTB, it could not be the purpose of the merger, agreed by the CEO of the BusinessDrom, Pavel Samiev. Given the "large number of State banks, whose branches in many regions are often simply overlapping", the merger of some would have a positive impact on the sector, evaluated the analyst of the Finama, Igor Dodonov. As a result of the deal, "it is possible to optimize the retail network and management functions of the banks involved in the transaction, thereby saving costs", he believes. However, the configuration of the Russian banking sector will not fundamentally change, stressed the Dodons: the assets of the unifying banks will be smaller than those of Sberbank, more than 1.5 times larger, and the total capital will be more than double. If the consolidation of State banks was intended to optimize the management process, that trend was fully entitled to existence, pointed out Belíkov. Samiev, however, doubted that the merger would significantly improve the efficiency of the unified structure. "This is a controversial point. It does seem that there would be synergy by reducing duplicate functions, but the effect could be negligible, and that the costs of consolidation might not be much less than those of the individual banks, but the relative costs would grow at all," he explained. From the point of view of synergy, the option of joining a small bank with expertise in segments where the State Bank could reinforce its position would be most interesting, noted the director of the French branch of the British Consulting Company Aperio Intelligence George Volshin. The "opening" and the WTB are competitors in many areas. The synergetic effect is thus not obvious. It will occur in the event of a subsequent compression of the combined bank by significantly reducing duplicate costs, which is a social risk." In his view, under the current uncertainty, "any predictions about the reasonableness of the merger are based on speculation," and "baselines can be adjusted to any scenario." There are no legal restrictions on opening up to the VTB, the partner of the Pen & Paper Sergei Teacher's Bar. The bank's financial recovery procedure ended in the summer of 2019, and, de facto, it became "a full-fledged participant in the financial market. "For its association with the WTB Bank, subject to the general requirements of corporate law and that of the regulator, there are no legislative restrictions," says counsel. What can be done with "Open" beyond the Open Guide still considers the sale of the bank to be "priority and possible", even in the current economic environment. The Act can be transferred to investors "ready to make real money", says Zadornov's letter. The Top Management points to two market niches where the bank could continue to work. For example, it is proposed to consider the establishment of an "opening bank" for business development in Russia, as it already has experience with small businesses based on the Toka Bank. Another option is to turn "Open" into a bank to consolidate players whose owners "by changing economic conditions will not be able to pre-capitalize them". Both areas of specialization seem promising, and Samiev thinks: "The "Open" option in pre-capitalizing out-of-market players will in fact turn it into a bank for "dead bankers". It will be able to obtain the assets of owners who, under the current circumstances, do not see on their own the prospects for business development in Russia, but the portfolios themselves may be viable, and the client base may not be the worst." The choice of "opening" a more "focused" strategy is a good solution in the context of blocking sanctions, Voloshin believes. However, the option of involving other players in the pre-capitalization process was more risky, as shareholders in falling banks might not be in a better position to leave assets. In the medium term, this is unlikely, especially in the face of external pressure, says Belíkov. "I think the most appropriate option is to sell a pool of private investors who may want to split the bank into parts or disassembly it," he notes.

ru.header: В Москве начинается суд по делу о попытке убийства двух подростков
ru.content: Москва. 20 января. INTERFAX.RU - Кузьминский суд Москвы в конце января приступит к рассмотрению уголовного дела о покушении на убийство двух несовершеннолетних девочек 2006 и 2004 года рождения, сообщили "Интерфаксу" в пресс-службе Мосгорсуда."Предварительное слушание по уголовному делу в отношении Никиты Лебедева назначено на 24 января и будет проходить в закрытом режиме", - сказала представитель суда.Как установлено следствием, Лебедев в течение 2020 года, используя вымышленные имена страниц в социальной сети "ВКонтакте", знакомился с несовершеннолетними, которым предлагал за отдельную плату выполнять опасные для жизни и здоровья трюки на большой высоте, фиксировать их на фото или видеокамеру и отправлять ему как доказательство выполненной просьбы.Так, он уговаривал несовершеннолетних потерпевших висеть вниз головой из окон и крыш домов, что представляло реальную угрозу для их жизни. Лишь по счастливой случайности обошлось без жертв.По данным СК, "свои поступки Лебедев совершал в связи с наличием у него расстройства сексуального предпочтения".Лебедеву предъявлено обвинение по статье о покушении на убийство (по ч. 3 ст. 30, п. "а" ч. 2 ст. 105 УК РФ).
ru.summary: Мосгорсуд приступил к рассмотрению по существу дела об убийстве двух малолетних девочек в 2006 и 2004 годах рождения, совершенном группой лиц по предварительному сговору.

en.header: Erdogan threatened Greece with a march of "rabid Turks"
en.subheader: Turkish President Erdogan threatened Greek Prime Minister Mitsotakis with a march of "rabid Turks"
en.content: Turkish President Recep Tayip Erdogan warned the Greek Prime Minister, Kiriakos Mitsotakis, about the march of the "fucking Turks." On the contrary, he denied plans to strike Athens with a designed Typhoon missile if Greece "act wisely." Erdogan accused the country of arming its islands in the Aegean Sea. "Mitsotakis, you say there, there, there, there, but know that if you're wrong, the rabid Turks will march," Erdogan threatened. Material is being supplemented.
en.summary: Greek Prime Minister Alexis Tsipras has called on Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan to hold a "march of the Turks" in protest against austerity policies.

record.header: Erdogan told Zelensky about his readiness to contribute to the settlement in Ukraine
record.subheader: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan discussed by phone with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky the prospects for resolving the Ukrainian conflict, Anadolu reports.
record.content: On 20 January, INTERFAX.RU, the President of Turkey, Recep Tayip Erdoğan, discussed by telephone with the President of Ukraine Vladimir Zelensky the prospects for a solution to the Ukrainian conflict, Anadolu reports. In particular, Erdoğan noted "the readiness of Ankara for a diplomatic contribution to the long-term peace between Moscow and Kiev." He also expressed his condolences to Zelensky for the crash in Kiev of a helicopter carrying Denis Monastyrsky, head of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Ukraine.

ru.header: Эрдоган пригрозил Греции маршем «бешеных турков»
ru.subheader: Президент Турции Эрдоган пригрозил премьеру Греции Мицотакису маршем «бешеных турков»
ru.content: Президент Турции Реджеп Тайип Эрдоган предупредил премьер-министра Греции Кириакоса Мицотакиса о марше «бешеных турков»Он отрицает планы по нанесению удара по Афинам с помощью разработанной ракеты Typhoon, если Греция будет «действовать по-умному». Эрдоган обвинил страну в том, что та вооружает свои острова в Эгейском море.«Мицотакис, ты говоришь то там, то сям, но знай, что если ты ошибешься, то бешеные турки пройдут маршем», — пригрозил Эрдоган.Материал дополняется.
ru.summary: Премьер-министр Греции Алексис Ципрас призвал президента Турции Реджепа Тайипа Эрдогана провести «марш турков» в знак протеста против политики жесткой экономии.

en.header: Ripple CTO Explains Why XRP Is a Commodity
en.subheader: Ripple CTO David Schwartz claims that the controversial XRP cryptocurrency meets the definition of a commodity
en.content: Ripple CTO David Schwartz recently took to Twitter to explain why XRP meets the definition of a commodity.He claims that it is a raw good that trades in commerce, with each XRP token being treated as equal to any other token. Moreover, no part of the cryptocurrency's value is derived from another party's legal obligations to XRP holders.Cryptocurrencies have frequently been referred to as securities or commodities, but the actual legal status of digital assets is far from being clear.To help determine which type of asset cryptocurrencies are, many turn to the Howey Test which was created by the U.S. Supreme Court in 1946 and defines the criteria for a security instrument. The test consists of three parts: whether there is an investment of money in a common enterprise with a reasonable expectation of profits; whether the profits come from the efforts of a promoter or third party; and if so, whether those efforts constitute an essential element of the scheme.If cryptocurrency meets all three criteria outlined by Howey, then it can be categorized as a security. In other words, if someone purchases cryptocurrency with the expectation that their investment will yield profits due to the efforts of another party (such as its issuer), then they are considered to own a security. This could mean that buyers would fall under securities regulations such as registration requirements and fraud prevention measures.The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission took Ripple to court in late 2020. The suit alleges that Ripple and its top two executives, Brad Garlinghouse and Chris Larsen, have been engaged in an "ongoing unregistered digital asset security offering" involving XRP since 2013. According to the SEC’s complaint, Ripple, Garlinghouse, and Larsen raised a combined $1.38 billion through unregistered sales of XRP tokens without registering them as securities
en.summary: Ripple CTO David Schwartz claims that the controversial XRP cryptocurrency meets the definition of a commodity. He claims that it is a raw good that trades in commerce, with each XRP token being treated as equal to any other token. No part of the cryptocurrency's value is derived from another party's legal obligations to XRP holders.

record.header: Huge XRP Transfers Occurred After Brad Garlinghouse's Statement on XRP's Importance
record.subheader: Massive bags of XRP tokens have been transferred after Ripple CEO gave some optimistic interviews in Davos
record.content: Popular crypto tracking platform Whale Alert has reported that, in the past 17 hours, several large transfers of XRP have been made, including one that may be considered "huge."Prior to that, the news media spread the word about Ripple chief executive Brad Garlinghouse making positive statements in Davos about XRP and sharing his expectations regarding the end of the lawsuit between Ripple and the SEC.Close to 357 million XRP on the moveThe aforementioned crypto tracker spotted four big XRP transactions, one of them carrying a mind-blowing amount of this Ripple-affiliated token – a total of 261,094,839 XRP evaluated at $102,414,350.This massive lump was moved between two anonymous wallets over 15 hours ago with no sign of addresses that belong to any crypto exchange, according to data provided by XRP explorer Bithomp.🚨 🚨 🚨 🚨 🚨 🚨 🚨 🚨 🚨 🚨 261,094,839 #XRP (102,414,350 USD) transferred from unknown wallet to unknown wallethttps://t.co/d9zPVrOLYj— Whale Alert (@whale_alert) January 19, 2023The rest of the transfers carried 34,700,000; 33,000,000 and 28,000,000 XRP. Here, Bitso crypto exchange, a unicorn based in Mexico and one of Ripple's major On-Demand Liquidity (ODL) partners, moved 34,700,000 XRP internally as it has often been doing recently, as it is actively spreads the usage of OLD in Latin America.The other two lumps of XRP were shoveled by whales from Bittrex exchange to Bitstamp and Bitso.Ripple CEO makes bullish statement on XRP in DavosAs reported by U.Today earlier, during the recent World Economic Forum in Davos that began on Jan. 16 and is to end today, Jan.20, Ripple chief Brad Garlinghouse gave several interviews, sharing his take on the much-expected potential end of the legal suit against Ripple from the SEC and XRP token.In particular, he stated that since the lawsuit began during the last few days of 2020, Ripple signed up a lot of new customers, who did not fear the possible consequences of the court decision, and the majority of them was outside the U.S. With billions of transactions made by Ripple monthly, XRP helps run over 50% of them. Many XRP users on Twitter took this as a positive signal, although the coin remains in the $0.39 price range.Brad stated that all the necessary materials have been submitted and briefed for the judge, and now she will take as long as necessary to make a decision. Garlinghouse does not expect a settlement with the SEC to happen, but he expects the end of the suit to take place in the first half of this year, or at least before the end of 2023.Overall, Garlinghouse stated that despite the current bear market, he is bullish on crypto in the long run and would like to stay away from any short-term price predictions. The utility of crypto, he believes, is going to grow fast.

en.content: Nazarbayev suffered from heart surgery, Peskov called for a focus on Putin's words about mobilization, China resumes group tourism in Moscow. On 20 January. INTERFAX.RU, a short summary of events that took place during the day: - Peskov called for a focus on Putin's words on partial mobilization. Commenting on the Administration's wording that "the action of the decree is continuing," he said: "I think it's more likely that this is a legal feature. I'm not ready to answer you now. I'm going to clarify the situation." The press secretary of the President of the Russian Federation referred the Russian Ministry of Defence to the issue of the introduction of the ZDC on the roof of an office building. In the Kremlin, the conflict around Ukraine was marked by an "upward spiral."-Platon's tariff would grow by 30 centimetres as of 1 February: from the current 2.54 roubles per kilometre to 2.84 rubles. Rosautdor published in July 2022 a planned indexation forecast, according to which a 44-cop increase was expected in February 2023.- The former President of Kazakhstan, Nursultan Nazarbaev, had had a heart surgery. It was planned, the heart of Nazarbaev was working on its own, without a pacemaker, reported by the Director of Surgery of the National Scientific Cardio-surgery Centre of Kazakhstan, Yuri Py.-China announced the resumption of group tourism, including to Russia, with effect from 6 February. record.header: What happened in the world of technology in a week. Evening Digest
record.subheader: One of the main topics of the outgoing week was still the massive cuts in IT giants.
record.content: Moscow. January 20, INTERFAX.RU - One of the main themes of the week away was still massive cuts in IT-giants. The dismissal of some of its employees was decided this time by Microsoft, Alphabet and Intel. Meta (recognized extremist in the Russian Federation and prohibited by IF) decided to sue an Israeli company, suspecting it of collecting and selling personal data from its social media networks. Experts report the worst numbers of smartphones delivered in a decade, and the new chapter of the bankrupt FTX hopes to revive the cryptobirus. Microsoft confirmed the intention to fire some 10,000 people from the American IT-giant Microsoft Corp. Wednesday confirmed plans to reduce the workforce by some 10,000 employees previously reported by the media with links to sources. Less than 5 per cent of the company's employees are affected by the dismissals, wrote the head of Microsoft, Satya Nadella, on a corporate blog, so the company expects "to adjust its spending pattern to income" and to focus on areas where demand is high. Microsoft is expecting a one-time cost of layoffs of $1.2 billion in the second fiscal quarter. Bloomberg reports that large cuts are also being prepared by Alphabet Inc., Google's parent company. The company will reduce the workforce by 6 per cent, which is about 12,000 jobs.A week's MarketWatch reported a reduction of another technogiant – Intel. The company will reduce over 500 jobs in California. Other large IT companies, including Meta Plants, Amazon.com Inc. Intel Corp. According to Layoffs.fyi, since the beginning of 2023, 25,000 people working in the technology sector have lost their jobs in the United States alone. Meta has sued an Israeli company because of the sale of personal data, Meta has sued the Israeli company Voyager Labs, accusing it of collecting and selling personal data from users of its Facebook and Instagram (both blocked in Russia), reported the Arstechnica portal.com. As stated in Meta, Voyager Labs developed a special software for Security Software Software to hide its activities from Meta. As a result, the defendant created and used over 38,000 Facebook fairy accounts to collect data on over 600,000 people, including posts, barks, lists of friends, comments, and statements in Meta. Among Facebook users who were able to gather data from an Israeli company were non-profit organizations, universities, media companies, medical institutions, the U.S. Armed Forces, and other citizens.In the UK, the management of IT companies for threats to children online.The British Government has amended the Internet Security Bill to Parliament, which provides for up to two years of imprisonment for IT company top managers for child online security violations, provides a competerworld.com. The punishment may threaten to ignore the requirements of the Online Safety Bill, in particular the risks of serious harm to children. Online Safety Bill has been working since 2019 to protect Internet users from fraudulent and other potentially dangerous content and, in particular, to prevent children from having access to harmful materials. However, frequent amendments to the document have led to criticism by the industry: business believes that many elements of the law are inoperable and could harm the British technology sector; the world ' s supply of smartphones at the end of 2022 was the worst in a decade. The world ' s smartphone supply in the fourth quarter of 2022 fell by 17 per cent, compared to the same period in the previous year - the worst in a decade, as shown by data from Canallys ' analytical company, while Apple ' s share in the smartphone market in the last quarter of the year was record (25 per cent), despite the difficulties caused by quarantine in China ' s assembly plants. Samsung (20 per cent) followed by Xiaomi (11 per cent), OPPO (10 per cent) and Vivo (8 per cent). "The fourth quarter and only 2022 by smartphone manufacturers were the worst in a decade", comments by analyst Canalys Runar Bjoorhovde. According to him, vendor problems were caused by declining demand and supply difficulties. Over the entire 2022 period, supplies dropped by 11 per cent, to 1.2 billion units. Samsung was the largest supplier. There were leaks in the Mailchimp service and Norton LifeLock. Mailchimp ' s popular mailing service reported a loss of user data, the second in six months, wrote the TechCrunch portal. The attack was identical to the previous one. According to the company, the compromise of internal systems resulted from an attack using social engineering, where fraudsters lured the victims ' data through telephone or e-mail. They then used stolen Malchimp passwords and accessed 133 user accounts. The company notified clients whose data were affected by the leak. A similar method was used in an attack last August. 214 users were compromised. Another leak that became known this week occurred in Norton LifeLock, which provides information security services. Thousands of accounts were damaged. Potential perpetrators could gain access to customer password managers. According to Gen Digital, Norton LifeLock ' s parent company, the result was a leak from other services rather than a break-in of the company ' s internal systems, so the victims were those who used the same passwords everywhere. It is believed that 6,450 Norton clients who were notified of the leak could suffer. CoO FTX allowed Kryptobirgi New Chapter FTX, John Ray, stated that he was exploring the possibility of reinitiating bankrupt cryptobirgia, reports The Wall Street Journal. In his first interview following the appointment of FTX in November, Ray announced that he had set up a working group to explore the possibility of restarting FTX.com, the company ' s main international exchange. He said that despite the fact that FTX top managers were subject to malpractice, "some clients appreciated their technology and suggested that rebooting the platform would be useful." Last November, the FTX cryptized exchange initiated bankruptcy under article 11 of the U.S. Bankman-Frid bankruptcy code. Uber is working on the development of an electric car for taxis and delivery.Uber is negotiating with car manufacturers to produce his own electric car, and told The Wall Street Journal by the CEO of Dar Hosrovshahi. He didn't name the specific car manufacturers, but last year Uber showed a prototype taxi with a British startup called Arrival. He said that new models would specialize in delivery services and taxis. The maximum speed in passenger transport vehicles will be lower than usual, as this "is not necessary for driving in the city", Hosrovshahi explained. The taxi seats will be in front of each other. The vehicles for delivery will be smaller in size and will be represented by two- and three-wheeled vehicles with a trunk. Apple postpones the release of AR points, but plans to present the garrison of mixed reality.Apple plans to present its first garrison of mixed reality this year, but postpones the release of AR points (AR - augmented reality, updated reality), Bloomberg reports with reference to sources. The delay is caused by technical problems, indicates a portal. AR-points may appear in 2024 or even early 2025, although the company originally intended to present them immediately after the hybrid reality garrison. The cost of the expensive version of the mixed reality garrison can be about $3,000. The price is justified by more expensive screens, more than 10 cameras, sensors, a powerful M2 processor, and a cheaper model with components similar to that in iPhone is planned. At the bottom of the more accessible version, Apple will compete with Meta's $1,500 garrisons. Patent applications also show two versions: Trademarks on Reality Pro and Reality One. As Bloomberg points out, the development of a hybrid reality garrison is easier because it uses virtual reality displays and only simulates the AR effect. Unlike the added reality points, which are more complex in the design.

ru.header: Что произошло за день: пятница, 20 января
ru.subheader: Назарбаев перенес операцию на сердце, Песков призвал ориентировать на слова Путина о мобилизации, Китай возобновляет групповой выездной туризм
ru.content: Назарбаев перенес операцию на сердце, Песков призвал ориентировать на слова Путина о мобилизации, Китай возобновляет групповой выездной туризмМосква. 20 января. INTERFAX.RU - Краткая сводка событий, произошедших за день:- Песков призвал ориентироваться на слова Путина в вопросе частичной мобилизации. Комментируя формулировку администрации о том, что "действие указа продолжается", он заявил: "Думаю, что скорее всего, это такая юридическая особенность. Не готов сейчас точно вам ответить. Уточню и тогда проясню ситуацию". Пресс-секретарь президента РФ переадресовал Минобороны РФ вопрос о появлении ЗРК на крыше ведомственного здания. В Кремле отметили развитие конфликта вокруг Украины "по восходящей спирали".- Тариф "Платона" с 1 февраля вырастет на 30 копеек: с текущих 2,54 рубля за километр до 2,84 рубля. Росавтодор в июле 2022 года публиковал плановый прогноз индексации, в соответствии с которым в феврале 2023 года предполагалось повышение тарифа на 44 копейки.- Бывшему президенту Казахстана Нурсултану Назарбаеву сделали операцию на сердце. Она была плановой, сердце Назарбаева работает самостоятельно, без кардиостимулятора, сообщил директор по хирургии национального научного кардиохирургического центра Казахстана Юрий Пя.- Китай объявил о возобновлении с 6 февраля группового выездного туризма, в том числе в Россию. Ассоциация туроператоров России сообщила о росте числа запросов на летние туры в Россию со стороны китайских туристов, первые группы ждут уже в феврале.- Криптовалютный брокер Genesis объявил о банкротстве. В документах, поданных компанией в суд, говорится, что число ее кредиторов превышает 100 тысяч, а ее задолженность перед 50 крупнейшими клиентами - около $3,4 млрд.- Даниил Медведев выбыл из Australian Open. Он потерпел поражение от представителя США Себастьяна Корде в третьем круге турнира.

record.header: The sale of the property of the daughter of the former deputy mayor of Moscow has been extended until July 24
record.subheader: The Moscow Arbitration Court has extended the sale of the property of the bankrupt ex-president of the Lights of Moscow Bank, the daughter of the former vice-mayor of Moscow, Maria Roslyak, for six months.
record.content: On 20 January, INTERFAX.RU, the Court of Arbitration of Moscow, extended the sale of the property of the bank's declared bankrupt ex-President Ogny Moscow, daughter of the former vice mayor of Moscow, Maria Roslák, for a period of six months. The next report of the financial manager of Eugenia Semchenko on the bankruptcy procedure was appointed on 24 July, reports to the court's website. On 14 August 2017, the capital arbitration, on the application of the development capital bank, recognized Roslak as bankrupt; the court then included in the creditor registry its debt to the development capital bank, amounting to approximately 24.9 million roubles.5 On December 2017, the court included in its creditor registry the Proford Investments Limited claim of 354 million roubles, and on 22 December 2017, the Ogny Moscow claim of 6,027 million roubles. In February 2016, the Basman Court of Moscow sentenced Roslyak to four years' imprisonment in the case concerning the embezzlement of the Bank of Ogny Moscow, which was suspended for 14 years because of the pregnancy of the convicted person and the presence of two minor children. The Fires of Moscow lost their licence in May 2014. In June 2014, the Court of Arbitration of Moscow declared the Bank to be bankrupt and appointed the AV to be a competitive manager. Roslák, daughter of Yuri Roslák, who in 1995-2010 was Deputy and First Deputy Mayor of Moscow, then Senator, Auditor of the Court of Accounts, CEO of Roskosmosmos and Deputy Director of the Khruníkov Centre.

ru.content: Прокуратура Берлина начала предварительное расследование в отношении «Русского дома» (Russisches Haus), пишет Tagesspiegel.Деятельность центра науки и культуры проверяется на предмет нарушения закона о внешней торговле и платежах, сообщил представитель ведомства Себастьян Бюхнер. Других деталей он не привел.Как пишет издание, жалобу в прокуратуру подал бывший депутат бундестага (1994-2017 гг.) от «Зеленых» Фолькер Бек.Материал дополняется.

en.header: An EU official said Brussels had no evidence of Iran supplying missiles to Russia
en.subheader: The European Union has no evidence of Iran supplying ballistic missiles to Russia, a senior European official told reporters.
en.content: Moscow. On 20 January, INTERFAX.RU - the EU has no evidence of Iran's supply of Russian ballistic missiles, declared to journalists a high-ranking European official. "We have no evidence that Iran is supplying Russia's ballistic missiles", said the source on Friday in Brussels, commenting on the anonymous agenda of the forthcoming meeting of the EU Foreign Affairs Council on Monday to discuss the situation in Iran. "But we have a lot of evidence on (the Russian Federation-IF) drones, but not missiles," added a media interviewer. He said that the EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs, Joseph Borrel, in every contact with the Iranian authorities, warned them that identifying Russia's missile supplies would have a negative impact on the EU's attitude towards Iran. "But at the moment: no - we have no evidence", was summarized by an EU official. On the eve of the day, the European Parliament adopted a resolution calling for the expansion of restrictive measures against Iran, because the euro deputies believe that Tehran continues to supply Russian unmanned aerial vehicles and plans to deliver ground-to-ground missiles.
en.summary: The EU has no evidence that Russia is supplying ballistic missiles to Tehran, said EU Foreign Minister Federica Mogherini.

record.header: The EU is studying the legal aspects of the idea of using frozen assets of the Russian Federation for Ukraine
record.content: Moscow. January 20th. INTERFAX. RU - The idea of the confiscation of Russian assets frozen in the West requires deep legal work in order to rebuild Ukraine, has been told to journalists by a high-ranking European official. "As regards frozen assets and whether they can be used, legal discussions are under way. There are many related legal problems," said the source in Brussels on Friday, commenting on the anonymity of the EU Foreign Council meeting on 23 January, one of whose main items will be EU assistance to Ukraine. "Some have already moved along this path, but for our part we are still studying the legal aspects before moving in any direction," added an EU member. Responding to a question, he said that the Ministers for Foreign Affairs would decide whether to discuss the topic at their meeting on the coming Monday, but he did not know that.

ru.header: Чиновник ЕС заявил об отсутствии у Брюсселя доказательств поставок Ираном ракет России
ru.subheader: Евросоюз не имеет доказательств поставок Ираном баллистических ракет России, заявил журналистам высокопоставленный европейский чиновник.
ru.content: Москва. 20 января. INTERFAX.RU - Евросоюз не имеет доказательств поставок Ираном баллистических ракет России, заявил журналистам высокопоставленный европейский чиновник."В настоящий момент у нас нет доказательств, что Иран поставляет баллистические ракеты России", - сказал источник в пятницу в Брюсселе, комментируя на условии анонимности повестку дня предстоящего в понедельник заседания Совета ЕС по иностранным делам, на котором будет обсуждаться ситуация в Иране."Но зато у нас много доказательств по (поставляемым РФ - ИФ) дронам. Но не по ракетам", - добавил собеседник СМИ.По его словам, высокий представитель ЕС по иностранным делам Жозеп Боррель при каждом контакте с иранскими властями предупреждает их о том, что выявление поставок ракет России отрицательно скажется на отношении Евросоюза к Ирану. "Но в данный момент: нет - мы не имеем доказательств", - резюмировал функционер ЕС.Накануне Европейский парламент принял резолюцию, в которой призвал расширить ограничительные меры против Ирана, поскольку евродепутаты полагают, что Тегеран продолжает поставлять России беспилотные летательные аппараты и планирует поставить ракеты класса "земля-земля".
ru.summary: ЕС не располагает доказательствами того, что Россия поставляет Тегерану баллистические ракеты, заявил глава МИД ЕС Федерика Могерини.

en.header: IFC managing director urges Ukraine to continue land reform
en.content: MOSCOW. Jan 20 (Interfax) - The International Finance Corporation (IFC), part of the World Bank Group, will keep supporting Ukrainian agribusiness companies, while the continuation of a land reform would make this support easier and provide companies with access to different financing, Ukrainian media quoted IFC Managing Director Makhtar Diop as saying.Speaking at the Ukraine House on the sidelines of the World Economic Forum in Switzerland's Davos, Diop suggested it is time to continue working on the necessary decrees and other documents to put the relevant laws into effect.The IFC has signed a consultative agreement on public-private partnership with the Ukrainian Finance ministry, which is important in that it would help attract a lot of private investment in the Ukrainian agrarian sector and provide a legal basis facilitating such investment, he said.The IFC also stands ready to provide trade financing and working capital and work on payment and IT solutions, which enhance the sector's efficiency by taking advantage of Ukraine's very high IT potential, he said.Rostislav Shurma, deputy head of the Ukrainian presidential office, said the Verkhovna Rada has registered legislation to be passed within two months at the longest, which would make it possible "to transform land from agricultural into industrial using just one electronic application to make this process very simple and not requiring any clearance."At the present time, if a land owner wishes to build even a small facility to produce meat, biofuel, or oil, they need to have an industrial plot of land, while the procedure of converting lands from one category to another is very complicated, Shurma said.
en.summary: The IFC has signed a consultative agreement on public-private partnership.

record.header: Atomic, green energy, grid de-centralization to be priorities of Ukraine's post-crisis energy sector - deputy energy minister
record.content: MOSCOW. Jan 20 (Interfax) - The Ukrainian energy sector will focus its post-crisis development on the atomic and green energy generation and a de-centralized power grid, Ukrainian Deputy Energy Minister for European Integration Yaroslav Demchenkov said."The three chief priorities in the development of our energy system is the accelerated development of the atomic, green energy and the construction of a de-centralized power grid. These priorities will be the basis of our updated energy strategy for the upcoming decades," the Ukrainian media quoted Demchenkov as saying at a discussion at the Ukraine House on the sidelines of the World Economic Forum in Davos on Thursday.In his words, the Ukrainian Energy Ministry is holding consultations with international partners on these issues."We are planning to stop using coal for power generation by 2040, while its role will be significantly reduced as early as after 2032. We are expecting the share of renewable energy in the energy balance to reach 25% in 2032 and to double by 2050," Demchenkov said, speaking of Ukraine's objectives.In his words, the shift away from coal will be conducted simultaneously with the construction of new solar and wind generation facilities, alongside new thermal power plants to run on bio-fuel.Ukraine is planning to build two nuclear reactors and to launch pilot projects of low-capacity reactors by 2032, he said.This is the right time to discuss Ukraine's future energy projects with international partners and investors in order to accelerate the energy transition after the end of the crisis, Demchenkov said. He also said he believes that energy transition in Europe would be impossible without Ukraine.EnergyPrioritiesUkraine

en.header: EU foreign ministers won't discuss new Russia sanctions at Council meeting on Jan 23 - official
en.content: BRUSSELS. Jan 20 (Interfax) - The European Union's Foreign Affairs Council (FAC) will not discuss new sanctions on Russia on January 23, a high-ranking EU official told journalists in Brussels on Friday.Speaking to journalists on the condition of anonymity to inform them of the agenda of a FAC meeting on Monday, the official said that, while he was confident that the member states have some ideas regarding sanctions, he could not comment on sectors to which they could apply.Nine Russia sanction packages are currently in effect, and the EU is focused on their proper application and on countering attempts to circumvent them around the world, the official said. While the EU is planning to study options for new sanctions, this is not expected to happen at the FAC meeting on Monday, the official said, adding that he was not in a position to say exactly when this could happen.At the same time, the official said the events in Ukraine and the EU's assistance to Kiev, including military assistance, would be among the top priorities on the Council of the EU's agenda.AgendaCouncilDiplomacyeconomic sanctionEU
en.summary: New sanctions not expected to be discussed at FAC meeting on Monday, official says.

record.header: The foreign ministers of the EU countries will not discuss new sanctions against Russia at their council on January 23
record.subheader: The EU Foreign Affairs Council will not discuss the next sanctions against Russia on January 23, a senior EU official told reporters in Brussels on Friday.
record.content: Moscow. On 20 January, INTERFAX.RU, the EU Foreign Affairs Council on 23 January, will not discuss the next sanctions against Russia, declared to journalists in Brussels a high-ranking EU official. "I am sure that member States have ideas about sanctions, but at this point I do not comment on the sectors that may fall under them," he said, introducing media representatives to the agenda of the Monday meeting of the heads of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the EU countries. "To date, nine sets of sanctions have been applied. We are focusing our attention on their correct application and on combating the circumvention of these sanctions worldwide. And we're going to explore the possibility of introducing new sanctions, but this Council has no provision for this on Monday, and I can't tell you when that will happen," the EU official answered the question, but he said that one of the main items on the EU Council's agenda would be Ukraine's events and EU assistance, including military assistance.
